To grow it is to plant a small joke and a generous bloomer at once, both fully committed to delight.

description: Blaze is one of the most widely planted red climbing roses in American history, introduced by Jackson & Perkins in 1932 and still beloved today. Producing clusters of medium-sized bright scarlet-red semi-double flowers on canes reaching 10 to 14 feet, it blooms profusely in spring with lighter repeat through summer and fall. Exceptionally cold-hardy through USDA Zone 4, Blaze has draped countless American porches, fences, and arbors for nearly a century.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Blaze' is a bright scarlet-red climbing rose bred by American breeder J. H. Nicolas in 1932, a cross between 'Paul's Scarlet Climber' and 'Gruss an Teplitz'. Its vivid scarlet semi-double blooms in huge clusters, repeat-flowering habit, and vigorous hardy climbing growth made it the most widely planted red climber in North America for decades.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Blaze' is a bright scarlet-red climbing rose bred by American hybridizer Jean-Henri Nicolas at the Jackson & Perkins nursery in New York, released in 1932 from a cross between the once-blooming climber 'Paul's Scarlet Climber' and the hybrid perpetual 'Gruss an Teplitz'. The cultivar made a sensation by combining the startling fire-engine red color of its climbing parent with genuine repeat bloom, producing abundant clusters of semi-double scarlet blooms on vigorous canes reaching three to four meters. Nicolas' 'Blaze' quickly became the most widely planted red climber in North American home gardens and remained so for fifty years.

A later-improved selection called 'Blaze Improved' or 'Improved Blaze' with better disease resistance has largely replaced the original in commerce. Light scent; remarkably cold-hardy into zone 4.

Its exceptional cold hardiness made it especially popular across the Midwest and Northeast, and it remains widely available at American garden centers nearly a century after introduction.
name_origin: Cultivar name evokes the flaming scarlet-red blooms that blaze across arbors and fences in spring.

description: Bonica is a classic light-pink landscape shrub rose producing clusters of 2 to 3 inch fully double pink blooms continuously on a rounded 3 to 5 foot bush. Lightly fragrant with excellent disease resistance, it was the first shrub rose to win AARS in 1987 and was inducted into the World Rose Hall of Fame in 2003, a foundational American landscape rose.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Bonica' is a soft pink shrub rose bred by French breeder Marie-Louise Meilland in 1981, the first shrub rose ever to win the All-America Rose Selections award (1987). Arching canes carry abundant clusters of small double pink blooms continuously; red-orange hips follow autumn flowers, and the plant is exceptionally disease-resistant and hardy.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Bonica' (also sold as 'Bonica 82' and 'Demon Rose') is a soft pink shrub rose bred by French hybridizer Marie-Louise Meilland at the Meilland nursery near Antibes, released in 1981 from a cross involving Rosa sempervirens, 'Mlle Marthe Carron', and 'Picasso'. The arching shrubby plant carries abundant small fully double clear pink blooms in large clusters continuously from late spring to heavy frost, and bright orange-red hips ripen in autumn and persist into winter. 'Bonica' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1987, the first shrub rose ever to take the top American honor, and the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2003.

The cultivar thrives without spraying in zones 4 to 9, tolerates partial shade, and helped establish the modern landscape-shrub-rose category alongside later 'Knock Out' introductions. Won AARS in 1987 as the first shrub rose to do so, paving the way for the landscape rose revolution.
name_origin: Named 'Bonica' as an Italian-style diminutive of 'bonne' (French for 'good'), meaning 'little beauty.'

A garden classic that quietly changed what a useful rose could look like.

description: Boscobel is a David Austin English rose introduced in 2012, producing perfectly formed coral-salmon rosette blooms with a rich myrrh fragrance accented by hawthorn, elderflower, pear, and almond. Growing 4 feet in an upright tidy shrub, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall with strong disease resistance. A modern Austin rose with uniquely complex fragrance beloved in American English-rose gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Boscobel' is a rich salmon-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2012, named for the seventeenth-century Boscobel House in Shropshire where Charles II hid in an oak tree after defeat at Worcester. Dense rosette-shaped blooms in warm coral-salmon tones with a strong myrrh fragrance bloom continuously on a compact upright plant.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Boscobel' is a warm salmon-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2012 from proprietary parentage. Austin named the cultivar for Boscobel House in Shropshire, the seventeenth-century hunting lodge where the future Charles II hid in the branches of the Royal Oak on 6 September 1651 while escaping Parliamentary forces after his defeat at the Battle of Worcester. The densely packed rosette-shaped blooms, eight centimeters across, open warm salmon-pink with deeper coral-red centres and soft apricot undertones, an unusually warm coloring in the Austin range.

A strong distinctive fragrance combines myrrh, almond, and old-rose notes. The compact upright plant reaches 1.2 meters, blooms continuously, and shows notably good disease resistance.

A mid-career Austin cultivar that has become a reliable garden favorite. Its complex hawthorn-elderflower-pear fragrance and strong disease resistance have made it a favorite modern Austin rose.

description: Brass Band is a warm apricot-peach floribunda rose producing clusters of 4-inch ruffled blooms in tones of apricot, peach, and melon on a 3 to 4 foot bush. history_text_short: Rosa 'Brass Band' is a warm apricot floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer Jack E. Christensen at Armstrong Roses in California, released in 1993 from a complex cross involving 'Gold Badge', 'Zorina', and 'First Edition'.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Brass Band' is a warm apricot floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer Jack E. Christensen at Armstrong Roses in California, released in 1993 from a complex cross involving 'Gold Badge', 'Zorina', and 'First Edition'. The clusters of fully double ruffled blooms open rich apricot-orange with coral undertones, fading gently to warm peach as flowers age, set against glossy dark green foliage on a vigorous upright plant. A sweet fruity fragrance complements the warm color.

'Brass Band' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1995, bringing genuine apricot-peach tones into the floribunda class where pure warm colours had been rare, and has since parented several further warm-toned floribundas. Long-lasting cut flowers and continuous garden bloom keep it popular.

Bred by Jerry Christensen at Jackson & Perkins and introduced in 1993, winning AARS in 1995. Named for the lively fanfare of a brass band, it brought vibrant apricot-peach tones into mainstream American rose gardens in the mid-1990s.

description: Carefree Beauty, also known as 'Katy Road Pink,' is a classic rose-pink shrub rose bred for the harsh American Midwest, producing 4-inch semi-double blooms continuously on an arching 4 to 5 foot bush. Famously cold-hardy, disease-resistant, and an Earth-Kind designated rose, it remains one of the best low-maintenance pink roses in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Carefree Beauty' is a medium-pink shrub rose bred by Dr. Griffith Buck at Iowa State University in 1977, part of his program for hardy disease-resistant roses for the American upper Midwest. Semi-double pink blooms, continuous repeat, and Zone 4 winter survival made it a landmark Buck rose.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Carefree Beauty' is a warm medium-pink shrub rose bred by Dr. Griffith Buck at Iowa State University in Ames, released in 1977 from a cross between an unnamed seedling and 'Prairie Princess'. Dr. Buck spent decades breeding roses specifically for the Midwestern climate, selecting for disease resistance, own-root vigour, and survival through USDA zone 4 winters without elaborate protection, and 'Carefree Beauty' became one of his signature successes. The semi-double blooms appear in clusters of three to fifteen, each a clear warm pink fifteen centimeters across with twenty to twenty-five petals, with a moderate sweet tea-rose fragrance.

Red-orange hips ripen in autumn. The cultivar is also sold as 'Katy Road Pink' from plants found growing along a Texas country road decades after Buck's introduction.

Griffith Buck at Iowa State University and introduced in 1977 as part of his 'tough-as-nails' Midwest-hardy rose program. Designated an Earth-Kind rose by Texas A&M for its extraordinary landscape performance without chemical inputs.
name_origin: Named 'Carefree Beauty' to convey both its beautiful blooms and its carefree low-maintenance habit.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Carefree Wonder' is a medium-pink shrub rose bred by the Meilland family in France in 1990, released in the Carefree series to continue Dr. Buck's legacy of hardy disease-resistant roses. Semi-double bright pink blooms with white reverses appear continuously on rounded dense plants ideal for hedging, and it won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1991.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Carefree Wonder' is a medium-pink shrub rose bred by French hybridizer Alain Meilland at the Meilland nursery, released in 1990 from proprietary parentage and marketed in North America by Conard-Pyle as part of the Carefree series that continued the low-maintenance landscape-rose tradition begun by Dr. Griffith Buck. The semi-double blooms open a cheerful medium pink with creamy-white reverses and a yellow centre, appearing continuously in clusters from late spring through heavy frost on rounded, dense, disease-resistant plants ideal for informal hedging and mass landscape plantings. 'Carefree Wonder' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1991.

Light scent; red-orange autumn hips add winter interest; cold hardy into zone 4 without protection, and reliable in containers and as a specimen. Bred by Meilland in France and introduced in 1991 by Conard-Pyle, winning AARS the same year.

Part of the Carefree series of low-maintenance landscape roses that helped pave the way for Knock Out's later dominance.

description: Climbing Cecile Brunner, also called the Sweetheart Rose, is a vigorous heirloom climbing rose producing thousands of perfectly formed thimble-sized pale pink double blooms with a soft sweet fragrance. The climbing sport can reach 20 feet or more, covering arbors, walls, and old trees in cascades of tiny roses each spring with lighter repeat bloom. An iconic cottage and heritage rose in American and English gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Cecile Brunner', sometimes called the sweetheart rose, is a delicate pink polyantha rose bred by French breeder Joseph Pernet-Ducher in 1881 from a cross involving Rosa multiflora. Tiny perfectly formed miniature hybrid-tea-shaped buds open to soft pink blooms a few centimetres across, and the rose has been a cottage-garden favourite for nearly 150 years.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Cecile Brunner', the sweetheart rose, is a polyantha rose bred by French hybridizer Joseph Pernet-Ducher at his Lyon nursery in 1881 from an unrecorded seedling of Rosa multiflora crossed with the tea rose 'Madame de Tartas'. Pernet-Ducher named the cultivar for the daughter of a friend in Switzerland. The plant produces enormous panicles of delicate small flowers, each a tightly rolled miniature hybrid-tea-shaped bud opening to a shell pink rosette two to four centimeters across with a sweet tea-rose fragrance.

Victorian and Edwardian florists used the tiny buds for boutonnières, corsages, and sweetheart bouquets. A climbing sport discovered in 1894 became one of the most vigorous climbers ever bred.

'Cecile Brunner' remains a cottage-garden favorite 145 years after introduction, treasured for its refinement and old-world charm. The shrub form was bred by Mme Marie Ducher in France in 1881 and named for Cecile Brunner, daughter of the Swiss family Brunner, famous rosarians of the era. The climbing sport appeared in 1894 and became the favorite 'Sweetheart Rose' for American Victorian brides' boutonnieres and countless cottage garden arbors.
name_origin: Named for Cecile Brunner, daughter of the Swiss Brunner family who ran a prominent Zurich nursery; historically called the 'Sweetheart Rose' for its small boutonniere-perfect form.

symbolism_story: The Cecile Brunner Rose can symbolize sweet love, its small blush-pink blooms long worn as the chosen Victorian boutonniere flower at weddings and afternoon parties. Another layer is heirloom grace, for the climbing form has been threading itself through cottage-garden trellises since 1894. In the modern garden, Cecile Brunner is the gentle, almost old-fashioned voice in the rose chorus, a sweet small flower whose meaning was decided more than a century ago and has not really changed.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Cherish' is a coral-pink floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer William A. Warriner at Jackson & Perkins in Medford, Oregon, released in 1980 from a cross between 'Bridal Pink' and 'Matador'. Unlike typical floribundas with many flowers per cluster, 'Cherish' often produces blooms singly on long stems, each a classic high-centered flower of salmon-coral-pink, so refined in form that many gardeners grow it as a hybrid tea. 'Cherish' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1980, and continued to win exhibition awards for its ability to produce exhibition-quality blooms with minimal disbudding.

Light tea fragrance. The compact upright plant blooms continuously through the season and remains a favorite for cut flowers and small-garden plantings. Bred by William Warriner at Jackson & Perkins and introduced in 1979, winning AARS in 1980.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Chrysler Imperial' is a dark red hybrid tea rose bred by Dr. Walter Lammerts in California in 1952, named after the Chrysler luxury car. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Chrysler Imperial' is a dark red hybrid tea rose bred by American hybridizer Walter Lammerts at the Germain Seed and Plant Company in California, released in 1952. The cross between 'Charlotte Armstrong' and 'Mirandy' produced classic high-centered blooms of deep crimson with up to fifty velvety petals and an intense old-rose and damask fragrance. Named after the Chrysler Imperial luxury car as part of an early cross-promotional arrangement, the cultivar won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1953, the American Rose Society's David Fuerstenberg Prize in 1956, and the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 1965.

Though newer cultivars have better disease resistance, 'Chrysler Imperial' remains a sentimental favorite in American gardens and is the parent of many later red hybrid teas.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Cupcake' is a medium-pink miniature rose bred by American amateur hybridizer Mark C. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Cupcake' is a medium-pink miniature rose bred by American amateur hybridizer Mark C. Spies and released by Justice Miniature Roses in 1981. Its parentage combines 'Gene Boerner' with a seedling involving 'Rumba' and 'Over the Rainbow'.

description: Dainty Bess is an unusual single-flowered hybrid tea rose from 1925, producing 3 to 4 inch soft pink single blooms with just 5 petals surrounding showy burgundy stamens. Growing 3 to 4 feet tall, mildly fragrant, it is one of the few single hybrid teas still widely grown and a beloved heirloom in American gardens for its simple wildflower-like beauty.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Dainty Bess' is a single-flowered pink hybrid tea rose bred by English breeder W. E. B. Archer in 1925, a cross between 'Ophelia' and 'Kitchener of Khartoum'. With just five wavy soft-pink petals surrounding striking maroon stamens, it broke from the full-petalled hybrid tea norm and won the Royal National Rose Society's Gold Medal the year it was introduced.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Dainty Bess' is a single-flowered pink hybrid tea rose bred by English amateur hybridizer W. E. B. Archer, released in 1925 from a cross between 'Ophelia' and 'Kitchener of Khartoum'. The cultivar was revolutionary: hybrid tea breeding had fixed the high-centered many-petalled form as the modern ideal, but 'Dainty Bess' reverted to wide five-petalled single blooms of soft pink with wavy ruffled edges, centered on a striking tuft of maroon-purple stamens. Critics were enchanted, and the Royal National Rose Society awarded the Gold Medal in 1925 and the American Rose Society conferred the John Cook Medal in 1939.

'Dainty Bess' remains widely grown for its elegant simplicity and old-fashioned charm, and is regarded as one of the finest single-flowered hybrid teas ever bred. Archer in England and introduced in 1925.

One of the few surviving single-petaled hybrid tea roses, it remained popular through the Great Depression and World Wars when its simple charm suited American cottage gardens.
name_origin: Named 'Dainty Bess' for the delicate beauty of its simple five-petaled flowers.

description: Don Juan is a classic large-flowered climbing rose introduced in 1958, renowned for its richly fragrant deep velvety-red double blooms on long stems perfect for cutting. Growing 8 to 12 feet on vigorous canes with glossy dark green foliage, it produces flowers with strong old-rose perfume continuously from spring through fall. history_text_short: Rosa 'Don Juan' is a velvety dark red climbing hybrid tea rose bred by Italian breeder Michele Malandrone in 1958, a cross between 'New Dawn' seedling and 'New Yorker'. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Don Juan' is a deep velvety red climbing hybrid tea rose bred by Italian hybridizer Michele Malandrone, released in 1958 from a cross between a seedling of 'New Dawn' and 'New Yorker'. The long pointed buds open to classic high-centered blooms of deep velvety crimson with dark wine undertones, up to thirteen centimeters across, produced continuously from late spring to heavy frost. A powerful sweet damask fragrance carries across a garden on warm evenings.

The vigorous climber reaches three to four meters and produces canes stiff enough to support itself on pillars and small trellises as well as larger structures. Though less disease-resistant than modern landscape climbers, 'Don Juan' has been a perennial American favorite for over sixty years for its combination of classic hybrid tea form, rich color, and intense fragrance.

Bred by Michele Malandrone in Italy and introduced in 1958, Don Juan became an instant classic for its rare combination of true velvet-red color, strong old-rose fragrance, and reliable repeat blooming. It remains one of the most widely planted red climbing roses in American gardens and a florist favorite for long-stem cutting.
name_origin: Named for the legendary literary lover Don Juan, reflecting the rose's romantic velvety-red allure.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Double Delight' is a bicoloured hybrid tea rose bred by Herb Swim and A. Ellis in California in 1977, a cross between 'Granada' and 'Garden Party'. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Double Delight' is a bicoloured hybrid tea rose bred by American breeders Herb Swim and Arnold Ellis, released by Armstrong Roses in 1977. A cross between the fragrant 'Granada' and the creamy 'Garden Party', the cultivar produces large high-centered blooms whose creamy yellow-white petals develop brilliant strawberry-red blushing along the edges in proportion to sun exposure; greenhouse-grown flowers stay nearly white while garden blooms become vividly bicoloured. The strong spicy fragrance recalls old damask roses.

'Double Delight' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1977, earned the World Federation of Rose Societies' Hall of Fame induction in 1985, and remains one of the best-selling bicoloured roses worldwide, especially popular as a cut flower. Ellis in California and introduced in 1977 by Armstrong Nurseries, winning AARS the same year.

Renowned for its strong spicy fragrance and sun-responsive color change from white to red-edged.
name_origin: Named 'Double Delight' for its two pleasures: striking red-and-cream bicolor and intensely sweet spicy fragrance.

description: Double Knock Out is a fully double-flowered version of the original Knock Out, producing clusters of 3-inch fully double cherry-red blooms with the same disease resistance and continuous bloom on a 3 to 4 foot rounded bush. history_text_short: Rosa 'Double Knock Out' is a fully double cherry-red shrub rose bred by William J. Radler and released by Conard-Pyle in 2004 from an unnamed seedling crossed with 'Knock Out'. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Double Knock Out' is a fully double cherry-red shrub rose bred by William J. Radler and released by Conard-Pyle in 2004 from an unnamed seedling crossed with 'Knock Out'. The cultivar was developed to answer one of the commonest criticisms of the original 'Knock Out': its single semi-double flowers, while prolific, lacked the classic full rose form many gardeners wanted. 'Double Knock Out' retained the breakthrough disease resistance, continuous self-cleaning bloom, and cold hardiness of its parent while producing thirty-petal fully double cherry-red blooms reminiscent of old-fashioned roses.

It quickly joined 'Knock Out' as a top-selling landscape rose, and the Knock Out family now includes pink, blush pink, yellow, coral, rainbow, and white sports marketed under the same series name. Brought traditional rose flower form to the iconic Knock Out platform, expanding the family and further cementing Knock Out's dominance of the American landscape rose market.
name_origin: Named for its fully double flower form compared to the original semi-double Knock Out.

It is proof that resilience and beauty are not at odds, and that gardening can be made easier without becoming dull.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Drift Coral' is a dwarf groundcover shrub rose bred by the Meilland nursery in France and released in North America by Conard-Pyle as part of the Drift series. Like its sister cultivars, it was developed by crossing larger landscape groundcover roses with miniatures to produce compact plants about 45 centimeters tall and 75 centimeters wide that carry continuous clusters of small fully double blooms. 'Drift Coral' opens in warm coral-orange shades that fade through apricot-pink to cream as flowers age, giving plants multiple color tones simultaneously.

The cultivar preserves modern landscape-rose disease resistance against black spot and powdery mildew, blooms continuously without deadheading, and survives into USDA zone 4 without winter protection. Ideal for small gardens, container edges, slope plantings, and low border use. One of the most popular warm-toned Drift roses for American home gardens.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Drift Pink' is a dwarf groundcover shrub rose bred by the Meilland nursery in France and released in North America by Conard-Pyle in 2008 as part of the Drift series. Meilland developed the Drift roses by crossing full-size groundcover landscape roses with true miniatures, producing compact low spreading plants 45 centimeters tall and 75 centimeters wide that bloom continuously with clusters of fully double soft pink miniature-sized flowers. The series preserves the disease resistance, cold hardiness, and easy-care habit of modern landscape roses while suiting small gardens, container plantings, rock gardens, and front-of-border use.

'Drift Pink' has become one of the most popular low-maintenance roses for residential use alongside its coral, red, peach, apricot, popcorn, and sweet sister cultivars. The Drift series crossed full-sized groundcover roses with miniatures to create low-growing disease-resistant landscape roses perfect for modern small American gardens.

history_text_long:

history_text_short: Rosa 'Easy Going' is a warm yellow-apricot floribunda rose bred by English breeder Harkness Roses in 1996 as a sport of 'Livin' Easy'. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Easy Going' is a warm yellow-apricot floribunda rose discovered by Harkness in the United Kingdom in 1996 as a sport of 'Livin' Easy', also known in some markets as 'Fellowship'. It keeps the parent's easy-care floribunda habit while shifting the color from orange toward softer peach, apricot, and gold.

The clusters of ruffled semi-double blooms appear through the season above glossy disease-resistant foliage. Its light honeyed fragrance and rounded habit make it useful in small gardens, containers, and low-input rose beds.

Because it belongs to the same easy-care line as 'Livin' Easy', the cultivar fits the late-twentieth-century move toward landscape roses that ordinary gardeners could grow without elaborate spraying. Its value is not rarity, but cheerful reliability.

description: Eden, also sold as Pierre de Ronsard, is a French romantic climbing rose bred by Meilland in 1987 and voted the World's Favorite Rose in 2006. Producing heavy fully-cupped old-rose-style blooms in pale pink blending to cream with deeper pink hearts, it grows 8 to 12 feet and blooms repeatedly from late spring through fall. history_text_short: Rosa 'Eden' (also called 'Pierre de Ronsard') is a soft pink-and-cream romantica climbing rose bred by Jacques Mouchotte at the Meilland nursery in 1985. Huge old-fashioned cupped blooms with ruffled pink petals fading to cream on the outer edges made it the World's Favourite Rose in 2006, and it remains the most popular wedding-garden climber worldwide.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Eden' (also sold as 'Pierre de Ronsard' in honor of the sixteenth-century French poet, and 'Eden Climber' in some markets) is a climbing romantica rose bred by French hybridizer Jacques Mouchotte at the Meilland nursery near Antibes, released in 1985 from a complex cross involving 'Danse des Sylphes', 'Händel', and 'Kalinka'. The quartered fully double cupped blooms, up to twelve centimeters across and carrying over forty petals, open a rich creamy ivory with a rose-pink heart and soft pink flushing that deepens in cool weather, evoking the full-bodied form of French old-rose paintings. The cultivar was voted World's Favorite Rose by the World Federation of Rose Societies in 2006, one of the highest honours in the rose world.

Light old-rose fragrance. The moderately vigorous climber reaches three meters and is one of the most photographed roses in wedding and garden photography.
name_origin: Sold as Eden (evoking the Garden of Eden) in the US; original French name Pierre de Ronsard honors the 16th-century poet.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Elina' is a pale primrose-yellow hybrid tea rose bred by Northern Irish breeder Pat Dickson in 1984, a cross between 'Nana Mouskouri' and 'Lolita'. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Elina' (also sold as 'Peaudouce') is a pale primrose-yellow to ivory hybrid tea rose bred by Northern Irish hybridizer Pat Dickson of Dickson Roses in Newtownards, released in 1984 from a cross between 'Nana Mouskouri' and 'Lolita'. The large classic high-centered blooms open ivory with a lemon-yellow heart and fade to near white in hot weather, carried on exceptionally long straight stems clothed in glossy disease-resistant dark green foliage. 'Elina' swept European trials, winning the Royal National Rose Society's President's International Trophy, Gold Medals at Belfast and Dublin, the Edland Fragrance Medal, and induction into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2006.

Consistently rated among the top 20 hybrid tea roses worldwide. It is among the most widely grown yellow hybrid teas in Europe.
name_origin: Renamed 'Elina' internationally; original name 'Peaudouce' (French for 'soft skin') was a commercial partnership.

description: Europeana is a legendary deep dark-red floribunda rose producing large clusters of 4-inch fully double rosette blooms on a 3 to 4 foot bush with bronze-red new growth. A 1968 AARS winner and World Rose Hall of Fame inductee, it remains one of the best red floribundas for American gardens with outstanding color and mass display.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Europeana' is a dark red floribunda rose bred by Dutch breeder Gerrit de Ruiter in 1963. Huge trusses of deeply ruffled velvety crimson blooms with bronzy foliage won it the Gold Medal of The Hague in 1962 and the All-America Rose Selections award in 1968, setting a new standard for floribunda colour intensity.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Europeana' is a dark red floribunda rose bred by Dutch hybridizer Gerrit de Ruiter of De Ruiter's Roses, released in 1963 from a cross between 'Ruth Leuwerik' and 'Rosemary Rose'. The cultivar produces huge trusses of up to thirty flowers, each a deeply cupped fully double bloom of dark velvety crimson with ruffled petals, so heavy with flowers that side branches often need staking. New foliage emerges bronzy red, maturing to dark glossy green.

'Europeana' won the Gold Medal of The Hague in 1962, gold at Madrid in 1968, and the All-America Rose Selections award in 1968, revolutionizing the color intensity possible in floribundas. Light fragrance; best planted where the heavy flower clusters can be admired up close. Still widely grown in public rose gardens worldwide.

Bred by Gijsbert de Ruiter in the Netherlands and introduced in 1963, winning AARS in 1968. Inducted into the World Rose Hall of Fame in 2006. A benchmark red floribunda that established modern standards for cluster-flowered red roses in American landscapes.
name_origin: Named 'Europeana' to celebrate European rose breeding excellence and its international introduction.

symbolism_story: Rosa Europeana embodies passionate devotion, its deep dark-red rosette clusters glowing with the saturated color long associated with serious romantic feeling. Its excellence is recognized in the rose Hall of Fame, a floribunda whose performance has set the standard for the class. It is often read as a flower of acclaimed ardor, a rose whose meaning combines old-fashioned passion with the official judgment that some devotions are simply better expressed than others.

description: Flower Carpet Pink is a classic bright-pink groundcover shrub rose producing masses of 2-inch semi-double blooms on spreading 2 to 3 foot wide mounded plants. Extremely disease-resistant and continuous-blooming, the Flower Carpet series revolutionized American groundcover rose plantings when introduced in the late 1980s.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Flower Carpet Pink' is a groundcover shrub rose bred by German breeder Werner Noack in 1989, the first of the landmark Flower Carpet series designed for low-maintenance mass planting. Sprawling arching canes carry carpets of bright pink semi-double blooms continuously from spring to frost on nearly disease-free evergreen-looking plants.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Flower Carpet Pink' (German: 'Heidetraum', meaning heath dream) is a low spreading groundcover shrub rose bred by German hybridizer Werner Noack in Gütersloh, released in 1989 from a cross between 'Immensee' and 'Amanda'. It was the founding cultivar of the Flower Carpet series, designed explicitly for public landscape use: low-growing arching plants spread a meter or more wide and cover themselves continuously from late spring to heavy frost with bright pink semi-double blooms, require no spraying to remain nearly free of disease, and tolerate heat, cold, pollution, drought, and neglect. The series has since expanded to include red, white, coral, amber, and yellow sports and hybrids.

'Flower Carpet Pink' won multiple European trial gold medals and transformed mass landscape planting across Europe and North America. Bred by Werner Noack in Germany and introduced by Anthony Tesselaar in 1989.

Pioneered the modern groundcover rose category worldwide, winning over 20 major international awards and remaining a top-selling landscape rose in America.
name_origin: Named 'Flower Carpet' for the way flowers cover the low spreading plants like a living carpet.

description: Flower Carpet Red is a vivid red groundcover shrub rose producing masses of 2-inch semi-double blooms on spreading 2 to 3 foot wide mounded plants. Like its Flower Carpet siblings, it is extremely disease-resistant and continuous-blooming, adding bright red color to American groundcover plantings and low borders.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Flower Carpet Red' is a bright red groundcover shrub rose released by Werner Noack in the 1990s as a colour addition to the Flower Carpet series. It retains the series' low spreading habit, continuous bloom, and exceptional disease resistance, producing carpets of small semi-double cherry-red blooms suitable for slopes, borders, and mass landscape planting.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Flower Carpet Red' is a bright cherry-red groundcover shrub rose bred by Werner Noack and released by Noack Roses as a color addition to the groundbreaking Flower Carpet series. Like the original pink founding cultivar, 'Flower Carpet Red' sends out arching canes that spread a meter or more across low mounded plants, carrying abundant clusters of small bright red semi-double blooms continuously from late spring to heavy frost. The series' trademark qualities remain: outstanding resistance to black spot and powdery mildew with no spraying, tolerance of heat, drought, pollution, and cold into USDA zone 5, and the ability to bloom continuously without deadheading.

Widely used for slope stabilization, mass landscape plantings, and large containers; the smaller plant size suits informal garden edges. Bred by Werner Noack in Germany and introduced by Anthony Tesselaar as part of the Flower Carpet series expansion in the 1990s.

Extends the Flower Carpet color range to vivid red for American landscape designs.
name_origin: Named for the red color within the Flower Carpet groundcover rose series.

description: Fourth of July is the only climbing rose besides America to win the All-America Rose Selections award, introduced in 1999 by Weeks Roses and bred by Tom Carruth. Producing clusters of striking red-and-white striped semi-double flowers with a spicy apple fragrance, it grows 10 to 14 feet and blooms heavily from late spring through fall. A patriotic American climbing rose for Independence Day celebrations.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Fourth of July' is a striped red-and-white climbing rose bred by American hybridizer Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in Upland, California, released in 1999 from a cross involving 'Roller Coaster' and 'Altissimo'.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Fourth of July' is a striped red-and-white climbing rose bred by American hybridizer Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in Upland, California, released in 1999 from a cross involving 'Roller Coaster' and 'Altissimo'. The cultivar was named to mark the United States Independence Day and released to time with summer-season sales. The semi-double blooms, just ten to sixteen wavy petals around a central tuft of golden stamens, open in irregular flashing stripes of cherry red and creamy white, so large clusters resemble bursts of red-and-white fireworks.

A strong sweet apple-and-rose fragrance adds to the appeal. 'Fourth of July' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1999 and became the second climber in AARS history to receive the honor after 'America' (1976).

Vigorous to three meters; continuous bloom; good disease resistance. Its red-and-white stripes made it an instant American favorite for Independence Day plantings and patriotic garden displays.
name_origin: Cultivar name honors US Independence Day (July 4); red-and-white stripes evoke the American flag.

Named for July 4th, the United States' national holiday, it belongs on porches and pergolas where backyard fireworks once lit the sky. It is the rose for people who love a parade.

description: Fragrant Cloud is one of the most fragrant hybrid tea roses ever bred, producing coral-red 5-inch blooms with an overwhelmingly powerful damask-rose perfume. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall with dark leathery foliage, it won the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal and was inducted into the World Rose Hall of Fame in 1981, a benchmark fragrance rose for American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Fragrant Cloud' is a coral-red hybrid tea bred by German breeder Mathias Tantau Jr. in 1963, regarded as one of the most powerfully fragrant roses ever introduced. It won the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 1969 with a rich old-damask scent that carries metres across a garden.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Fragrant Cloud' (German: 'Duftwolke') is a coral-red hybrid tea rose bred by Mathias Tantau Jr. at Uetersen, Germany, released in 1963 from an unknown seedling crossed with 'Prima Ballerina'. The cultivar's strong, complex, spicy damask-and-citrus fragrance is regarded by many rosarians as the finest of any twentieth-century hybrid tea; a single bloom can scent an entire room. 'Fragrant Cloud' won the Royal National Rose Society's President's International Trophy in 1963, the American Rose Society's James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 1969, and induction into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 1981.

The blooms open coral-orange and gradually deepen to brick-red with age, and the plant is notably vigorous and disease-resistant. It remains an industry benchmark for rose fragrance.
name_origin: Named 'Fragrant Cloud' for the way its powerful perfume seems to envelop the garden like a cloud of scent.

description: Garden Party is a delicate ivory-white hybrid tea rose lightly blushed with pink, producing large 5-inch high-centered blooms with mild tea fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall with glossy foliage, this 1960 AARS winner bred by Herb Swim remains a beloved American garden rose for its soft romantic coloring and reliable repeat bloom.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Garden Party' is a creamy white hybrid tea rose bred by Herb Swim in California in 1959, a cross between 'Charlotte Armstrong' and 'Peace'. The elegant high-centred blooms show a soft pink flush at the petal edges, inheriting 'Peace' coloration. It won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1960 for exceptional form and garden performance.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Garden Party' is a creamy white hybrid tea rose bred by American hybridizer Herb Swim at Armstrong Roses in Ontario, California, released in 1959. The cross between the crimson 'Charlotte Armstrong' and the famous 'Peace' produced a cultivar inheriting its parent's refined form and subtle coloring: creamy-ivory petals with a delicate pink blush along the edges, opening from long elegant buds to high-centered blooms twelve centimeters across. The rose won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1960, and later became a parent in Swim's 1977 masterpiece 'Double Delight'.

'Garden Party' is valued for its vigorous upright growth, disease resistance, and the way its shade-loving creamy flowers light up evening gardens. Light fruity fragrance.

Bred by Herb Swim at Armstrong Nurseries in California, introduced in 1959 and winning AARS in 1960. Remains a staple in American rose catalogs for over six decades.
name_origin: Named 'Garden Party' to evoke elegant social gatherings in classic American gardens.

description: Gertrude Jekyll is David Austin's most fragrant rose, introduced in 1986, voted the Nation's Favorite Fragrant Rose in the UK and treasured for its rich true old-rose damask perfume. Producing fully-quartered rich pink rosette blooms on an upright 4 to 5 foot shrub, it blooms repeatedly from late spring through fall. The essential oil is distilled for perfume production. A cornerstone fragrant rose in American English-rose collections.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Gertrude Jekyll' is a strong pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 1986, named for the pioneering English garden designer. Quartered rosette-shaped deep pink blooms carry the quintessential old-damask fragrance that Austin describes as the definitive old-rose scent, and it won the American Rose Society's Gamble Fragrance Medal in 2002.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Gertrude Jekyll' is a strong pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 1986 from a cross between 'Wife of Bath' and the Portland rose 'Comte de Chambord'. Austin named the cultivar for Gertrude Jekyll (1843-1932), the influential English garden designer and writer who, with Edwin Lutyens, defined the Arts and Crafts garden. The quartered rosette-shaped blooms, eight to ten centimeters across with up to eighty petals, open a strong rich rose-pink and carry what Austin's company calls the quintessential old-rose fragrance: the classic heavy damask perfume that has been distilled for attar-of-roses for centuries.

The cultivar won the American Rose Society's James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 2002, and the English oil-distillation industry has trialled it as a commercial perfume source.
name_origin: Named for Gertrude Jekyll (1843-1932), pioneering English garden designer and writer who shaped modern perennial border design.

symbolism_story: The Gertrude Jekyll Rose can symbolize artful devotion, named in honour of the pioneering English garden designer whose color theory still shapes mixed borders today. Another layer is perfume grace, for its old-rose fragrance has been distilled commercially for rose oil, a rare crossover between ornamental and industrial perfumery. To grow Gertrude Jekyll is to keep a quiet tribute in the garden, a flower that joins the memory of a great designer with one of the most generous scents in modern roses.

description: Gold Medal is a tall deep-yellow grandiflora rose tinged with orange and red on petal edges, producing 4 to 5 inch high-centered blooms on 5 to 6 foot stems. Strongly fragrant with a tea-apple scent, this 1983 Jackson & Perkins introduction is considered one of the best yellow grandiflora roses ever bred for American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Gold Medal' is a golden yellow grandiflora rose bred by Jack Christensen at Armstrong Roses in 1982, a cross between 'Yellow Pages' and ('Granada' x 'Garden Party'). Long pointed buds open to high-centred deep yellow blooms lightly flushed coral on the petal edges, and the cultivar remains one of the finest yellow grandifloras for cutting and exhibition.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Gold Medal' is a deep yellow grandiflora rose bred by American hybridizer Jack E. Christensen at Armstrong Roses in Ontario, California, released in 1982 from a complex cross involving 'Yellow Pages', 'Granada', and 'Garden Party'. The long pointed buds open slowly to classic high-centered blooms of warm golden yellow with coral-pink flushing along the petal edges, a coloring unusual among yellow roses and prized by exhibitors. Tall upright growth, glossy disease-resistant foliage, and exceptionally long straight stems make 'Gold Medal' a premier cut-flower rose and a reliable performer in hot climates where many yellows fade.

Light tea and fruit fragrance. The cultivar has won several regional trials and remains among the best-selling yellow grandifloras in North America.

Bred by Jerry Christensen at Armstrong Nurseries in California and introduced in 1982 by Jackson & Perkins. Named for its rich gold petal color, it has won multiple international gold medals and became one of the most widely planted yellow grandifloras in American gardens.
name_origin: Named 'Gold Medal' for both its rich golden flower color and the international medals it won in rose trials.

description: Golden Celebration is a David Austin English rose introduced in 1992, producing some of the largest blooms in the Austin range — magnificent deep golden-yellow cupped flowers with a strong Tea, Sauternes wine, and strawberry fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet in a graceful rounded shrub, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall. A showstopper golden rose for American cottage gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Golden Celebration' is a rich golden-yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 1992, one of his largest-flowered introductions at up to fourteen centimetres across. Deeply cupped luminous gold blooms with strong tea-rose-and-Sauternes fragrance appear continuously on arching shrubs that can be trained as short climbers in warm climates.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Golden Celebration' is a rich golden-yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 1992 from a cross between 'Charles Austin' and 'Abraham Darby'. The deeply cupped fully double blooms are among the largest of any English Rose, reaching fourteen centimeters across with a hundred petals, opening in luminous rich golden yellow and carrying a complex strong fragrance that combines classic tea rose with notes of Sauternes wine and strawberry. The arching vigorous shrub reaches 1.5 meters and blooms continuously, and in warm climates the long flexible canes can be trained as a short climber reaching three meters.

'Golden Celebration' has won several international awards and remains one of the most popular yellow Austin roses, beloved for the extraordinary size and color intensity of its blooms. Bred by David Austin and introduced in 1992, Golden Celebration marked a breakthrough for Austin in combining truly rich deep-golden color with old-rose cupped form and powerful fragrance.

It remains one of the most beloved yellow English roses in American cottage gardens and English-style rose collections.
name_origin: Cultivar name celebrates the brilliant golden-yellow color and the rose's showstopping large-bloom display.

uses_list.text: Large golden blooms release rich tea fragrance around sunny seating areas

Among David Austin's English roses, it is also famous for an unusual fragrance of Sauternes wine and crushed strawberries — a scent rare even in a fragrant tribe. This is the rose for gathered tables and happy occasions, a flower that smells, as much as looks, like a quiet act of festivity.

description: Golden Showers is a classic All-America Rose Selections winner from 1957, bred by Walter Lammerts in California, producing large fragrant clear-yellow semi-double flowers that fade to cream on canes reaching 8 to 10 feet. One of the few truly yellow climbing roses that repeat blooms reliably from spring to frost, it remains a signature yellow climber in American gardens for trellises, walls, and pergolas.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Golden Showers' is a bright yellow climbing rose bred by Dr. Walter Lammerts at Germain Seed and Plant Company in California, released in 1956 from a cross of 'Charlotte Armstrong' and 'Captain Thomas'. Loose semi-double blooms open golden yellow and fade to cream, winning the 1957 AARS award.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Golden Showers' is a bright yellow climbing rose bred by American hybridizer Dr. Walter Lammerts at the Germain Seed and Plant Company in California, released in 1956 from a cross between 'Charlotte Armstrong' and 'Captain Thomas'. The cultivar produces loose semi-double to lightly double blooms opening rich golden yellow and fading gradually to lemon and cream with age, carried singly or in small clusters on long straight stems. The plant is a moderate-vigour climber, reaching three meters with stiffer canes than typical climbers, which lets it work well on pillars and small trellises as well as larger structures.

'Golden Showers' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1957 and the Portland Gold Medal, and it remains the top-selling yellow climbing rose in North America over sixty years later. Moderate sweet tea-rose fragrance.
name_origin: Cultivar name evokes the cascading display of golden-yellow flowers tumbling from trellises like showers of gold.

symbolism_story: The Golden Showers Rose carries joyful friendship, the yellow rose's traditional meaning of warm companionship lifted onto a climber's frame. Paired with the image of a golden cascade, its blooms shower down trellises and walls in pure gold. To plant it is to drape friendship itself over a structure — a vertical celebration of light, warmth, and the people who make a garden feel like home.

description: Graham Thomas is David Austin's breakthrough yellow English rose introduced in 1983, hailed as the first modern English rose to achieve true rich yellow color combined with old-rose cupped form and strong tea-rose fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet as a shrub or 8 to 12 feet as a climber, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall and set the standard for all yellow Austin roses to follow. A cornerstone of American English-rose gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Graham Thomas' is a golden-yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 1983, named for the horticulturist and old-rose champion Graham Stuart Thomas. Combining the fullness and fragrance of old roses with modern repeat bloom, its deep cupped yellow blooms helped launch the English Rose revolution and won the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2009.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Graham Thomas' is a golden-yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, Shropshire, England, released in 1983 from a cross between the climber 'Charles Austin' and a seedling involving 'Iceberg' and an unnamed yellow tea rose. Austin named the cultivar for the English horticulturist Graham Stuart Thomas, who had championed old roses through his writing and garden restoration work at Mottisfont Abbey. 'Graham Thomas' represented a breakthrough for the English Rose programme: rich golden-yellow color unavailable in traditional old roses, combined with the deep-cupped many-petalled form and powerful tea-rose fragrance of old roses, on a modern repeat-flowering shrub.

It quickly became one of the most widely sold roses in Britain and North America, won the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2009, and transformed public expectation of what modern roses could achieve. It was the first English rose to combine true rich yellow color with old-rose cupped form, launching the modern yellow English-rose lineage now central to American cottage gardens.
name_origin: Named for Graham Stuart Thomas (1909-2003), British rosarian and garden writer who revived interest in old garden roses.

description: Heritage is one of David Austin's most beautiful English roses, introduced in 1984, producing perfectly shell-shaped soft pink cupped blooms of exquisite old-rose form with a rich lemony-myrrh fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet as a well-branched shrub, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall. history_text_short: Rosa 'Heritage' is a soft blush-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 1984, a cross involving 'Wife of Bath' and an iceberg seedling. Perfectly symmetrical cupped pale pink blooms carry a strong lemon-and-honey fragrance, and the cultivar is widely regarded as one of the most beautifully formed English Roses Austin ever bred.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Heritage' is a soft shell-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 1984 from an unnamed seedling crossed with a seedling of 'Iceberg' and 'Wife of Bath'. The rose is widely considered one of the most flawlessly formed English Roses ever bred: the deeply cupped blooms, up to ten centimeters across with forty to fifty petals, open in perfect symmetry to show a soft pure shell-pink deepening slightly toward the centre, and the flowers age gracefully without blowing apart. A strong distinctive fragrance combines lemon, honey, and old-rose notes.

The upright bushy plant reaches 1.5 meters, blooms continuously, and shows good disease resistance. 'Heritage' won the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 2004, and remains a signature Austin cultivar in specialty rose gardens worldwide.

Bred by David Austin and introduced in 1984, Heritage was celebrated as one of the most elegant rose forms ever created, winning numerous awards internationally. Its shell-pink cupped blooms and distinctive lemon-myrrh fragrance have made it an iconic heritage rose in American cottage and formal gardens alike.

description: Home Run is a modern landscape shrub rose bred by Tom Carruth in 2005, a descendant of Knock Out with improved bloom color and heat tolerance. Growing 3 to 4 feet tall and wide, it produces clusters of vibrant true-red single flowers continuously from spring through hard frost, with exceptional resistance to black spot and powdery mildew. A top-performing no-spray landscape rose across American climates.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Home Run' is a bright scarlet-red shrub rose bred by American breeder Tom Carruth and Ping Lim for Weeks Roses in 2006, developed specifically to resist both black spot and downy mildew, diseases that affect even the original Knock Out rose. Single vivid red blooms cover the compact plant continuously on nearly disease-free foliage.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Home Run' is a scarlet-red shrub rose bred by American hybridizer Ping Lim at Bailey Nurseries in Minnesota and released through Weeks Roses in 2006 after extensive disease-pressure screening. 'Home Run' was developed specifically to resist downy mildew, a disease that can affect the otherwise extremely resistant Knock Out series, in addition to the standard black spot and powdery mildew targets of all modern landscape roses. The single five-petalled bright scarlet blooms, with a central boss of golden stamens and a white eye at the petal base, appear continuously in clusters from late spring to heavy frost on a compact mounded plant about 1.2 meters tall.

Selected for hot and humid southern gardens where downy mildew is most problematic, 'Home Run' requires no spraying, deadheading, or fussing. Bred by Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses and introduced in 2005, Home Run crossed Knock Out with Baby Love to combine top disease resistance with a truer red color and improved southern heat performance.

It has become a widely planted commercial landscape rose across the American South and West.
name_origin: Cultivar name evokes baseball triumph, celebrating its breakthrough disease resistance.

description: Hot Cocoa is a unique chocolate-brown and orange-red floribunda rose producing 4-inch ruffled blooms in clusters on a 3 to 4 foot bush. A 2003 AARS winner bred by Tom Carruth, it is one of the most distinctive smoky-toned roses in American gardens, with moist cocoa-colored petals that stand out in any planting.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Hot Cocoa' is a smoky chocolate-russet floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in Upland, California, released in 2002 from a complex cross of 'Altissimo' and 'Livin' Easy'.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Hot Cocoa' is a smoky chocolate-russet floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in Upland, California, released in 2002 from a complex cross of 'Altissimo' and 'Livin' Easy'. The cultivar broke new ground in rose color: buds open as rich chocolate-red and mature to smoky brown-russet with coral undertones, a palette unlike anything previously available in floribundas. Wavy ruffled petals, strong old-rose-and-spice fragrance, and vigorous upright growth made it an immediate sensation.

'Hot Cocoa' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 2003 (an honor for a color-breakthrough rose) and has since parented several further brown and russet cultivars. Excellent garden performer; clusters of large flowers bloom continuously on disease-resistant plants. One of the first roses to bring truly chocolate-brown tones into wide commercial cultivation, pioneering a new trend in novelty rose colors.
name_origin: Named 'Hot Cocoa' for the unique chocolate-brown to russet-orange color of the blooms.

It is the rose for those who would rather start a conversation than win a prize.

description: Iceberg is the world's most popular white floribunda rose, producing prolific clusters of semi-double 3-inch white blooms on a graceful 3 to 5 foot shrub. Lightly fragrant, almost continuous-blooming, and one of the most disease-resistant roses ever bred, it was inducted into the World Rose Hall of Fame in 1983 and remains a top American landscape rose.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Iceberg' is a pure white floribunda bred by Reimer Kordes in 1958, released in Germany as 'Schneewittchen' (Snow White). Profuse semi-double white blooms on disease-resistant plants made it the most widely planted white rose of the 20th century, inducted into the Rose Hall of Fame in 1983.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Iceberg' (German: 'Schneewittchen', meaning Snow White) is a pure white floribunda rose bred by German hybridizer Reimer Kordes of W. Kordes' Söhne, released in 1958 from a cross between 'Robin Hood' and 'Virgo'. The cultivar bears abundant clusters of semi-double pure white blooms with a light honey fragrance, repeating continuously from late spring to heavy frost, on exceptionally vigorous, disease-resistant plants that tolerate heat, cold, drought, and neglect far better than typical modern roses. 'Iceberg' won the Royal National Rose Society's President's International Trophy in 1958, the All-America Rose Selections award in 1983, and was voted the World's Favorite Rose by the World Federation of Rose Societies in 1983.

It remains perhaps the most widely planted white rose in the world. Inducted into the World Rose Hall of Fame in 1983 as the best-known white rose.

Remains a signature landscape rose of American public gardens, cottage plantings, and foundation beds.

description: Ingrid Bergman is a classic dark red hybrid tea rose producing 4 to 5 inch velvety deep-red blooms of perfect classic form on strong stems. Growing 3 to 4 feet tall with glossy dark green foliage, mildly fragrant and very disease-resistant, it was named World's Favorite Rose in 2000 and is beloved by American gardeners for its faultless form and rich color.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Ingrid Bergman' is a deep red hybrid tea rose bred by Danish breeder Niels Poulsen in 1984, named with permission from the estate of the Swedish film star. The velvety dark red blooms on vigorous upright plants won the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2000 and remain one of the most planted red roses in Europe.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Ingrid Bergman' is a deep red hybrid tea rose bred by Danish hybridizer Niels Dines Poulsen at Poulsen Roser, released in 1984 from an unnamed seedling lineage. Released by Poulsen the year after the death of Swedish-born actress Ingrid Bergman, the cultivar was named with permission of her family. The classic high-centered velvety dark red blooms do not fade or purple in sun, the plant is exceptionally disease-resistant and winter-hardy, and the cultivar quickly became one of the most planted red roses in Scandinavia and northern Europe.

'Ingrid Bergman' won Gold Medals at Belfast, Madrid, and The Hague, and was inducted into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2000. Light tea fragrance; excellent cut flower.

Bred by Poulsen Roser in Denmark and introduced in 1984 to honor Swedish film star Ingrid Bergman. Remains one of the most reliable and disease-resistant red hybrid teas on the market.

description: John F. Kennedy is a pure white hybrid tea rose producing 5 to 6 inch classic high-centered blooms with a mild licorice fragrance on strong stems. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall, this 1965 introduction honors President Kennedy and remains one of the most popular white commemorative roses in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'John F. Kennedy' is a white hybrid tea rose bred by Eugene Boerner at Jackson & Perkins in 1965, introduced shortly after the American president's death. Large greenish-white buds open to classic high-centred pure white blooms with a strong tea-rose fragrance, making it a longtime favourite memorial rose in gardens and cemeteries.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'John F. Kennedy' is a pure white hybrid tea rose bred by American hybridizer Eugene S. Boerner at Jackson & Perkins, released in 1965 from a cross of an unnamed seedling and 'White Queen'. Boerner, who had bred many famous American roses, worked with the Kennedy family to select and name the cultivar in memory of the assassinated president. The large shapely buds are faintly greenish in color, opening slowly to pure white high-centered blooms up to thirteen centimeters across with forty to fifty petals, carried on upright strong-stemmed plants.

A strong sweet tea-rose fragrance complements the pristine color. Light feeders who prefer warm climates, 'John F. Kennedy' has been widely planted in memorial gardens, civic plantings, and American cemeteries for sixty years.

Eugene Boerner at Jackson & Perkins and introduced in 1965, two years after the president's assassination. Chosen and approved by the Kennedy family as a tribute to the late president, it set a standard for pure white hybrid tea roses in America.

description: Joseph's Coat is a dazzling multicolor climbing rose bred by Armstrong and Swim in 1964, famous for blooms that open yellow, turn orange, and age to crimson red all on the same plant at once. Growing 8 to 12 feet on vigorous canes, it produces clusters of semi-double flowers from late spring through fall, creating a living tapestry of changing color. A showstopper for American arbors and large trellises.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Joseph's Coat' is a multicoloured climbing rose bred by American breeders Herb Swim and O. L. Weeks in 1964, a cross between 'Buccaneer' and 'Circus'. Each cluster shows flowers in every shade from gold to orange to crimson simultaneously, evoking the biblical Joseph's coat of many colours. It won the Bagatelle Gold Medal in 1964.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Joseph's Coat' is a multicoloured climbing rose bred by American hybridizers Herb Swim and O. L. Weeks at Armstrong Roses in Ontario, California, released in 1964 from a cross between 'Buccaneer' and 'Circus'. The cultivar was named for the biblical Joseph's coat of many colours because each flower cluster displays blooms in every stage of color transition simultaneously: buds open golden yellow, pass through orange, coral, and pink phases, and finish as deep crimson before dropping, so a single plant shows the full warm-color spectrum at once. The climbing plant reaches about three meters with semi-double blooms in continuous clusters from late spring to heavy frost.

'Joseph's Coat' won the Bagatelle Gold Medal in 1964 and the Madrid Gold Medal in 1966. Light tea fragrance; best on a pillar or short trellis where every color can be admired.

Bred by David Armstrong and Herb Swim at Armstrong Nurseries in California and introduced in 1964, Joseph's Coat was named for the biblical coat of many colors and dazzled American gardeners with its unprecedented color-shifting blooms. It remains one of the most beloved multicolor climbing roses in American gardens.

description: Jude the Obscure is a David Austin English rose introduced in 1995, famous for its exceptional guava and white wine fragrance — ranked among the most powerfully scented Austin roses ever bred. Producing pale yellow to apricot cupped blooms of incurved old-rose form on a tidy 4 to 5 foot shrub, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall. history_text_short: Rosa 'Jude the Obscure' is a deep cupped buff-yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 1995 and named for Thomas Hardy's 1895 novel. Incurved chalice-shaped blooms of pale buff yellow release an extraordinarily powerful fruity fragrance reminiscent of guava and sweet white wine, regarded as one of the strongest-scented English Roses.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Jude the Obscure' is a pale yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 1995 from proprietary parentage, named for Thomas Hardy's 1895 tragic novel Jude the Obscure set in the Dorset and Oxford countryside. The distinctly incurved cupped chalice-shaped blooms open pale buff-yellow with a richer warm-yellow heart, hiding their centres behind incurving outer petals, and carry one of the most intense fragrances in the entire Austin range, an extraordinary tropical fruit scent combining guava, sweet white wine, and old rose. Rose writers frequently rank it among the top three most fragrant English Roses ever bred.

The upright shrub reaches 1.2 meters and blooms continuously, though it needs careful placement in warm sunny gardens to fully develop the fragrance. Moderately disease-resistant.

Its exceptional tropical guava-and-wine fragrance made it an instant classic for fragrance-focused American rose gardens.

This is a flower for readers and romantics alike, a bloom whose name and perfume both linger in the memory long after the season ends.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Julia Child' is a butter-yellow floribunda rose bred by Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses, released in 2004 from proprietary parentage. Chef Julia Child personally selected the cultivar from Carruth's seedling rows a few years before her death, and the name was formally licensed by her estate. The clusters of fully double cupped blooms open a rich clear buttery yellow that holds its color in sun without fading to white, carried above glossy dark green foliage on a vigorous, compact, strongly disease-resistant plant.

A strong distinctive licorice and anise fragrance scents the garden. Named in her honor, proceeds support her charitable foundation. 'Julia Child' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 2006 and quickly became one of the best-selling yellow roses in North America, frequently ranked among the easiest yellows for home gardeners to grow well.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Just Joey' is a coppery-buff hybrid tea rose bred by English breeder Roger Pawsey of Cants of Colchester in 1972, a cross between 'Fragrant Cloud' and 'Dr. A. J. Verhage'. Named for Pawsey's wife Joey, its ruffled apricot-copper petals and strong fruity fragrance won it the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 1994.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Just Joey' is a buff-apricot hybrid tea rose bred by English hybridizer Roger Pawsey of Cants of Colchester, released in 1972 from a cross between 'Fragrant Cloud' and 'Dr. A. J. Verhage'. Pawsey named the cultivar for his wife Joey. The loosely ruffled blooms open from pointed coppery buds to wide wavy-edged flowers in shades of apricot, copper, and buff that deepen toward the petal edges, with a strong fruity fragrance inherited from 'Fragrant Cloud'.

The cultivar won numerous regional awards and was voted the World's Favorite Rose by the World Federation of Rose Societies in 1994, earning Hall of Fame status. Its informal, almost old-rose look and unique coloring have kept it popular in English cottage-garden and cutting-garden designs for over fifty years. Remains one of the UK's and America's most beloved apricot roses.
name_origin: Named 'Just Joey' by breeder Roger Pawsey for his father-in-law Joe Pawsey.

description: Knock Out is the best-selling landscape shrub rose in American history, producing clusters of 3-inch semi-double cherry-red blooms continuously from spring through frost on an incredibly tough 3 to 4 foot rounded bush. Disease-resistant, self-cleaning, and requiring no spraying, it revolutionized American home landscaping after its 2000 AARS win.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Knock Out' is a cherry-red shrub rose bred by amateur Wisconsin hybridizer William Radler and released by Conard-Pyle in 2000. Its nearly disease-free foliage, continuous bloom without deadheading, and cold hardiness revolutionized the American rose market and it became the best-selling rose in North American history.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Knock Out' is a cherry-red shrub rose bred by William J. Radler, an amateur hybridizer and horticulturist in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, over a fifteen-year programme targeting resistance to black spot disease. Conard-Pyle released the cultivar in 2000 from a proprietary cross, and it won the All-America Rose Selections award the same year. 'Knock Out' has remarkable qualities: near-complete resistance to black spot, powdery mildew, and rust; continuous self-cleaning bloom from spring to hard frost without deadheading; cold hardiness into zone 4; and vigorous compact growth needing no spraying.

Within a decade 'Knock Out' and its color sports became the best-selling roses in North American history, with over a million plants sold annually, transforming landscape rose use in public spaces, medians, and home gardens. Bred by William Radler in Wisconsin over 15 years of breeding and introduced by Conard-Pyle in 2000, winning AARS the same year.

The best-selling rose in American history by 2010, it transformed home landscaping by offering disease resistance without spraying, making roses accessible to millions of casual gardeners.
name_origin: Named 'Knock Out' for its knockout appearance in the landscape and ability to knock out rose disease problems.

description: Lady of Shalott is one of David Austin's most disease-resistant and vigorous English roses, introduced in 2009, producing chalice-shaped blooms in warm salmon-pink with orange undersides and a light fruity tea fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet in a robust healthy shrub, it blooms continuously from late spring through fall with exceptional weather resistance. history_text_short: Rosa 'Lady of Shalott' is a warm orange-apricot English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2009, named for Tennyson's poem. Loosely cupped chalice-shaped blooms open warm salmon-pink with golden yellow undersides, and the exceptionally disease-resistant plant is one of the toughest and most reliable later Austin introductions for beginners and tough climates.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Lady of Shalott' is a warm orange-apricot English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2009 from proprietary parentage as part of a deliberate breeding programme to produce more disease-resistant English Roses for the landscape market. Austin named the cultivar for the enchanted weaver in Alfred Tennyson's 1842 poem 'The Lady of Shalott'. The loosely cupped chalice-shaped blooms open warm salmon-pink on the inside with rich golden-yellow petal reverses, so the flower shows both colours simultaneously; a strong fragrance combines warm tea, clove, and soft apple notes.

The arching bushy plant reaches 1.2 meters, blooms continuously, and is among the most disease-resistant and cold-hardy English Roses yet bred, making it a popular choice for tough American and Scandinavian gardens as well as beginner gardeners seeking English Rose elegance without fuss. Bred by David Austin and introduced in 2009 for Austin's 50th anniversary, Lady of Shalott was named after Tennyson's famous 1833 poem of the same name.

Its robust health and disease resistance made it immediately popular in American gardens as a beginner-friendly Austin rose.
name_origin: Named for Tennyson's 1833 poem 'The Lady of Shalott', set in Arthurian Camelot.

Its meaning is romance touched by melancholy — a rose that flowers like a final, lovely scene, beautiful because it cannot last.

description: Louis Philippe is a classic Old Garden rose of the China class bred by Modeste Guerin in France in 1834, famous for its extraordinary repeat blooming in deep crimson-pink cupped double blooms with lighter pink centers. Growing 4 to 6 feet in an arching shrub, it blooms non-stop from spring through hard frost and thrives in southern American heat where many roses fail. The iconic cemetery rose of the American South, often called 'the Cracker rose' in Florida.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Louis Philippe' is a crimson China rose bred by French nurseryman M. Guerin in 1834 and named for King Louis Philippe I, the liberal Orleanist monarch who reigned from 1830 until the 1848 revolution.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Louis Philippe' is a crimson China rose bred by French nurseryman M. Guerin in 1834 and named for King Louis Philippe I, the liberal Orleanist monarch who reigned from 1830 until the 1848 revolution. Guerin's introduction reached the American South via French and Creole gardens in New Orleans, and planters carried cuttings across Texas and the Gulf states throughout the nineteenth century. The loosely double cupped blooms open deep crimson with lighter pink petal edges and white bases, continuously from late spring to heavy frost on a vigorous shrub reaching two meters.

Its tolerance of extreme heat, humidity, drought, and neglect allowed it to survive a century or more in abandoned Texas homesteads, and the Texas Rose Rustlers and other heritage-rose groups have repropagated it from countless old cemetery and ranch plantings. Light sweet scent.

Known as the 'Cracker rose' in Florida for its association with early settler homesteads, it remains the iconic Southern heirloom rose.
name_origin: Named for King Louis Philippe I of France (1773-1850), reigning during the rose's introduction.

symbolism_story: Louis Philippe Rose carries Southern heritage on its shoulders — the iconic crimson cemetery and homestead rose of the Gulf Coast, brought to Texas in 1839 and surviving in old yards long after the houses around its have fallen. Its endless bloom — a true non-stop repeat unlike most old garden roses — keeps its flowering from March to frost. It is the rose that outlived the antebellum South and kept blooming.

description: Macy's Pride is a hardy shrub rose from the Easy Elegance series bred by Ping Lim, bearing clusters of fragrant creamy-yellow semi-double flowers on a vigorous disease-resistant plant. Reaching 4 to 5 feet tall and wide with glossy dark green foliage, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall in USDA Zones 4 to 9. A popular low-care landscape rose for American gardens, a portion of sales historically supported Macy's breast cancer research fundraising.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Macy's Pride' is a cream-yellow shrub rose released by the Brownell family of New Hampshire as part of their hardy subzero rose program. Named for the American department store partnership, it offers ivory blooms with lemon-yellow centres on cold-hardy plants for northern gardens.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Macy's Pride' is a cream-yellow shrub rose released in the United States as part of the lineage of hardy subzero roses bred originally by Walter and Josephine Brownell in Rhode Island and extended through partnerships with major American retailers. The cultivar produces clusters of loosely double blooms that open creamy ivory with lemon-yellow centres and fade toward pure cream with age, carried on a compact upright shrub with dark green disease-resistant foliage. Like other roses in the subzero hardy tradition, 'Macy's Pride' was selected for the ability to survive harsh northern US winters with minimal dieback, continuous repeat flowering, and resistance to common fungal diseases.

The rose is frequently planted in public-garden trials and memorial collections in the northeastern United States. Introduced in 2007 as part of Bailey Nurseries' Easy Elegance series bred by Ping Lim, Macy's Pride was sold through Macy's department stores in partnership with breast cancer awareness campaigns.

It became a symbol of both modern landscape-rose breeding and American retail-driven cause marketing.
name_origin: Cultivar name honors Macy's department store, the original retail partner whose sales contribution supported pink-ribbon research.

description: Madame Plantier is a classic French Old Garden rose of the Alba-Noisette hybrid class, bred by Plantier in 1835, famous for her massive spring display of pure white fully-double rosette blooms with green button eyes and powerful sweet fragrance. Growing 6 to 10 feet in an arching once-blooming shrub, she carries a single spectacular bloom flush in late spring. An iconic heritage rose in American heirloom gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Madame Plantier' is a pure white hybrid alba-noisette rose bred by French nurseryman Plantier in 1835, once-blooming but prolific in a single spectacular early-summer display. Arching canes covered in creamy-white pompon blooms with a powerful old-rose fragrance make it a classic of nineteenth-century French rose gardens, still widely grown in heritage collections.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Madame Plantier' is a pure white hybrid rose bred by French nurseryman Plantier of Lyon in 1835, probably from a cross between a Rosa alba and a noisette rose (though exact parentage is lost). The arching flexible canes reach two to three meters and can be trained as a weeping shrub, pillar, or small climber. In early summer the plant produces a single but overwhelming display: hundreds of small fully double blooms open from greenish-cream buds to flat pompon-rosette-shaped pure white flowers with a powerful sweet old-rose damask fragrance, covering the plant for about three weeks.

Though once-blooming, the display is so spectacular that 'Madame Plantier' remains widely planted nearly two centuries later. Empress Josephine included it in the Malmaison collection shortly before her death, and it survives today in many nineteenth-century French rose gardens.

Bred by Plantier of Lyon, France in 1835 and widely distributed through the 19th century, Madame Plantier became a staple of American cemetery and farmstead plantings, where her hardy constitution and spectacular spring bloom made her a favorite heirloom rose still found surviving on abandoned homesteads across the American South.
name_origin: Named by breeder Plantier of Lyon for his wife Madame Plantier.

description: Marilyn Monroe is a creamy apricot-blush hybrid tea rose producing classic 5-inch high-centered blooms with a light tea fragrance on long stems. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall with dark green foliage and excellent disease resistance, this glamorous American rose has become a top cut flower and wedding rose since its 2002 introduction.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Marilyn Monroe' is a creamy apricot hybrid tea rose bred by Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in 2002, released with licensing approval from the Monroe estate. Long elegant buds open to classic high-centred blooms in shades of buff apricot with cream and coral tones, carried on long straight stems above disease-resistant foliage.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Marilyn Monroe' is a buff-apricot hybrid tea rose bred by American hybridizer Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in California, released in 2002 under licensing agreement with the Marilyn Monroe estate. The refined pointed buds open slowly to large high-centered blooms in subtle shades of creamy apricot, coral, and warm buff that deepen toward the petal edges, with a velvety satin finish suited to the name. Light tea-rose fragrance.

The plant is vigorous and disease-resistant for a hybrid tea, with long straight stems that make it a premium cut flower. 'Marilyn Monroe' became one of the most successful celebrity-named roses of the early twenty-first century, popular at wedding florists for its warm glamorous coloring and classic exhibition form.
name_origin: Named in 2002 for Hollywood icon Marilyn Monroe (1926-1962), evoking its timeless glamour.
