description: Mary Rose is one of David Austin's earliest and most reliable English roses, introduced in 1983, a workhorse of the modern old-rose revival. Producing loose rich pink cupped blooms with a pleasant honey-almond fragrance on a vigorous 4 foot shrub, it blooms continuously from late spring through fall and is exceptionally disease-resistant. A foundational Austin rose widely planted in American cottage gardens for decades.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Mary Rose' is a medium-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 1983, named for the Tudor warship raised from the Solent in 1982. Loosely cupped rose-pink blooms with honey-and-almond fragrance bloom continuously on a bushy reliable plant that became one of Austin's most popular introductions for cottage gardens.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Mary Rose' is a warm medium-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 1983 from a cross between 'Wife of Bath' and 'The Miller'. Austin named the cultivar to mark the raising of the Tudor warship Mary Rose from the seabed off Portsmouth in October 1982, an event of immense archaeological importance to Britain. The loosely cupped blooms open a warm rose-pink with a lighter reverse and a moderate fragrance blending honey, almond, and old-rose notes.

The dense bushy plant reaches 1.2 meters and flowers continuously from late spring to hard frost, with particularly reliable, heavy bloom and good disease resistance, making it one of the most dependable older English Roses for cottage and mixed borders. Two sports, the white 'Winchester Cathedral' and the soft pink 'Redoute', extend the series.

Bred by David Austin and introduced in 1983 to commemorate the raising of the Tudor warship Mary Rose from the seabed of the Solent in 1982. It was one of the foundational roses of Austin's early English-rose lineage and remains a proven performer in American cottage gardens for its reliability and continuous bloom.
name_origin: Named for the Mary Rose, Tudor warship of Henry VIII sunk in 1545 and spectacularly raised from the Solent seabed in 1982.

description: Red Meidiland is a French-bred groundcover shrub rose from Meilland International, producing carpets of single bright red flowers with white centers and golden stamens from late spring through fall. Growing 2 to 3 feet tall and spreading 4 to 6 feet wide, its low arching habit makes it ideal for slopes, mass plantings, and groundcover roles. Exceptionally disease-resistant and widely used in American commercial and municipal landscapes.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Meidiland Red' (also called 'Red Meidiland') is a low spreading groundcover shrub rose bred by the Meilland family in France in 1987. Small single cherry-red blooms with white eyes appear continuously in large clusters on dense low-mounded plants, one of the earliest successes of the Meidiland landscape series that pioneered the modern low-maintenance shrub-rose category.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Meidiland Red' (officially 'Red Meidiland', French: 'Rouge Meidiland') is a low-spreading groundcover shrub rose bred by Marie-Louise Meilland at the Meilland nursery near Antibes, France, released in 1987. It was part of the pioneering Meidiland series that Meilland launched in the mid-1980s to create extremely tough, self-maintaining landscape roses for parks, median plantings, and municipal use. The dense low-mounded plant spreads about 1.5 meters wide, carrying continuous large clusters of small single cherry-red blooms with white eyes and golden stamens from late spring to heavy frost.

Red-orange hips ripen in autumn and persist into winter. The Meidiland series as a whole (red, white, pink, coral, scarlet) preceded and in many ways anticipated the later Knock Out breakthrough in easy-care landscape roses.

Bred by Marie-Louise Meilland in France in the 1980s, Meidiland roses were developed for highway and public landscape use where no-spray, low-care performance was essential. Red Meidiland became one of the most widely planted landscape roses in American commercial plantings from the 1990s onward.
name_origin: 'Meidiland' is a Meilland trademark for the landscape rose series; 'Red' describes the flower color.

As a foundation of American municipal landscaping, it has earned a quiet honor as a true landscape workhorse. This is the rose of public spaces — bred for survival rather than show, yet faithfully producing red blooms summer after summer wherever it is planted and forgotten.

description: Mister Lincoln is a legendary dark red hybrid tea rose, producing richly fragrant velvety crimson blooms up to 5 inches across on long strong stems. Growing 5 to 6 feet tall with upright form and matte dark foliage, this 1964 All-America Rose Selections winner remains one of the most popular red roses in American gardens for its classic form and powerful damask fragrance.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Mister Lincoln' is a dark red hybrid tea rose bred by Herb Swim and O. L. Weeks in California in 1964, a cross of 'Chrysler Imperial' and 'Charles Mallerin'. Named for President Abraham Lincoln, it is prized for velvety crimson blooms and strong damask fragrance, winning the 1965 All-America Rose Selections award.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Mister Lincoln' is a dark red hybrid tea rose created by American rose breeders Herb Swim and O. L. Weeks in 1964 from a cross between the fragrant 'Chrysler Imperial' and the intense crimson 'Charles Mallerin'. Conard-Pyle launched the cultivar in the United States, and the rose won the 1965 All-America Rose Selections award for its exceptional garden performance. The long-stemmed velvety crimson blooms open from classic pointed buds to cupped flowers thirteen centimeters across, and the strong damask-rose fragrance carries across a garden on warm evenings.

Named for President Abraham Lincoln, it has remained among America's top-selling red hybrid tea roses for six decades, a benchmark for dark red rose fragrance. Unlike many modern reds, the cultivar has proven durable and disease-resistant in home gardens, and remains among the top-selling red hybrid teas sixty years after introduction.
name_origin: Named for American President Abraham Lincoln, honoring his leadership and legacy.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Munstead Wood' is a deep velvety crimson English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2007, named for Gertrude Jekyll's own Surrey garden. Deep cupped blooms of near-black crimson with rich old-rose fragrance and a compact habit suit small gardens, and the rose won the American Rose Society's James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 2016.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Munstead Wood' is a deep velvety crimson English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2007 from proprietary parentage. Austin named the cultivar for Munstead Wood, Gertrude Jekyll's own garden in Surrey designed in partnership with architect Edwin Lutyens, and Jekyll's garden spirit pervades the rose: opening crimson and deepening to a near-black-velvet dark red with subtle burgundy undertones as flowers age, held in deeply cupped rosette form. A strong warm blackberry-and-damson fragrance with blueberry hints complements the color.

The compact bushy plant reaches only 90 centimeters, making 'Munstead Wood' one of the smallest Austin roses and a favorite for small gardens and containers. It won the Royal National Rose Society's James Mason Gold Medal in 2011 and the American Rose Society's James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 2016.
name_origin: Named for Munstead Wood, the Surrey home and garden of Gertrude Jekyll, designed by Edwin Lutyens in 1897.

description: Nearly Wild is a classic American floribunda-type shrub rose introduced in 1941, producing single five-petal pink flowers with white centers and yellow stamens resembling wild species roses. Growing 2 to 3 feet tall and wide in a compact mounded form, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall and proves exceptionally hardy in USDA Zones 4 to 9. A beloved low-maintenance rose for American cottage gardens and informal landscapes.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Nearly Wild' is a single-flowered floribunda rose bred by American breeder E. S. Brownell in 1941, a cross between 'Dr. W. Van Fleet' and 'Leuchtstern'. Clusters of five-petalled clear pink blooms with yellow centres look like wild roses, bloom continuously, and remain one of the hardiest and most disease-resistant older floribundas for northern gardens.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Nearly Wild' is a single-flowered floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer Eugene Sanford Brownell at the Brownell nursery in Little Compton, Rhode Island, released in 1941 from a cross between the climber 'Dr. W. Van Fleet' and the polyantha 'Leuchtstern'. The Brownells bred subzero hardy roses for New England winters, and 'Nearly Wild' combined that hardiness with the informal charm of species roses: large clusters of wide five-petalled blooms, each a clear medium pink with creamy yellow bases and a tuft of golden stamens, cover the compact upright shrub continuously from spring to heavy frost. The cultivar tolerates partial shade, resists disease without spraying, and survives into USDA zone 4 without winter protection.

It remains a staple in cottage-garden plantings and heritage rose collections across the northeastern United States. Bred by Brownell in Rhode Island and introduced in 1941, Nearly Wild was among the first 'sub-zero' American shrub roses developed for New England winters.

It remains a widely planted low-maintenance rose in American cottage gardens for its effortless performance and wild-rose charm.
name_origin: Cultivar name reflects resemblance to wild species roses with its single five-petal form.

description: New Dawn is one of the most beloved climbing roses ever bred, a 1930 sport of Dr. W. Van Fleet that made history as the first patented plant in the United States. Producing masses of fragrant pale blush-pink double flowers on vigorous canes that reach 12 to 20 feet, it blooms repeatedly from late spring through fall and tolerates light shade better than most climbers. Widely grown on American arbors, pergolas, and fences.
history_text_short: Rosa 'New Dawn' is a pale pink climbing rose bred in the United States by Henry Dreer and patented in 1930 as the first plant patent ever granted in the United States. A repeat-flowering sport of 'Dr. W. Van Fleet', it blooms all summer with soft pink semi-double flowers, was inducted into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 1997.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'New Dawn' is a pale pink climbing rose discovered as an everblooming sport of the once-blooming climber 'Dr. W. Van Fleet' at the Somerset Rose Nursery in New Jersey, introduced by Henry A. Dreer in 1930. The cultivar earned a remarkable historical distinction: United States Plant Patent No. 1, issued August 18, 1931, the very first plant patent ever granted in the United States under the Plant Patent Act of 1930. Semi-double creamy blush-pink blooms with golden stamens appear in clusters from late spring to heavy frost, carried on vigorous long canes reaching six meters, on glossy disease-resistant dark green foliage.

A light sweet apple fragrance complements the soft color. 'New Dawn' was voted into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame as the World's Favorite Rose in 1997.

Van Fleet, New Dawn became Plant Patent No. It remains one of the most widely grown climbing roses in American gardens nearly a century later.
name_origin: Cultivar name reflects its breakthrough as a new repeat-blooming dawn for climbing roses and historical patent landmark.

Its meaning is a doubled dawn: a new era of horticulture and the soft daily light of a climbing rose against an old wall.

description: Old Blush is one of the oldest cultivated China roses in the Western world, introduced to Europe in 1751 and to America shortly after, producing medium pink semi-double blooms with a light sweet-pea fragrance. Growing 4 to 6 feet in an arching shrub, it blooms repeatedly from spring through frost and is a parent of countless modern roses. The famous 'last rose of summer' of Thomas Moore's 1805 poem and a cornerstone heirloom American rose.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Old Blush' (also called 'Parson's Pink China', 'Common Monthly', and 'Monthly Rose') is a pale pink China rose of uncertain Chinese origin, grown in China for centuries before Swedish East India Company ships carried it to European gardens around 1752.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Old Blush' (also called 'Parson's Pink China', 'Common Monthly', and 'Monthly Rose') is a pale pink China rose of uncertain Chinese origin, grown in China for centuries before Swedish East India Company ships carried it to European gardens around 1752. It is one of the legendary Four Stud Chinas, four repeat-flowering China roses imported between 1752 and 1824 that revolutionized Western rose breeding by introducing continuous bloom into the otherwise once-flowering European gene pool. Every modern repeat-flowering rose traces ancestry to these four.

The semi-double blooms, seven centimeters across, open a clear soft pink that deepens in sun, are carried in clusters almost continuously, and carry a light sweet-pea fragrance. 'Old Blush' is among the most vigorous and tolerant old roses, thriving with minimal care across zones 6 to 10 and surviving in neglected plantings for centuries.

Introduced to European gardens in 1751 from China, Old Blush revolutionized Western rose breeding by introducing the repeat-blooming trait to European roses, which until then mostly bloomed only once per year. It is a parent of countless modern roses and immortalized as 'The Last Rose of Summer' in Thomas Moore's 1805 poem.
name_origin: Named for the soft pink 'blush' color; also sold as 'Parsons' Pink China' for the English botanist who first grew it.

symbolism_story: Old Blush Rose is timeless constancy — this is the China rose that, on arriving in Europe in the late 1700s, first taught Western roses how to bloom more than once a season. Its quiet pink double flowers were immortalized as the last rose of summer in Thomas Moore's 1805 poem. It is the ancestress of every modern repeat-flowering rose, still in cultivation, still blooming on schedule.

description: Olivia Rose Austin is David Austin's most disease-resistant English rose, introduced in 2014 and named for his granddaughter. Producing medium pink cupped rosette blooms with a sweet fruity fragrance on a tidy 3 to 4 foot shrub, it blooms continuously from late spring through hard frost. Considered by David Austin himself as the best rose he had ever bred, a modern benchmark for American English-rose collections.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Olivia Rose Austin' is a soft pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2014 and named for his granddaughter. Austin called it possibly his most beautiful introduction, with rosette-shaped pale pink blooms, strong classic fragrance, and exceptional disease resistance.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Olivia Rose Austin' is a soft pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2014 from proprietary parentage and named for Austin's granddaughter Olivia. Austin reserved the highest family-name honor in his catalog for this rose, and in the catalog entries he described it as possibly the most beautiful English Rose he had ever bred. The perfect rosette-shaped fully double blooms, eight to ten centimeters across, open pure soft pink with a slightly deeper pink heart and age gracefully without turning blousy, carried on bushy upright plants 1.1 meters tall with notably disease-resistant dark green foliage.

A strong classic old-rose fragrance with a subtle hint of fruit complements the form. Austin selected the cultivar to be as easy to grow as a Knock Out while offering full English Rose form and scent.

David Austin publicly called it the best rose he had ever bred, and it has won the Royal National Rose Society's James Mason Gold Medal. It is widely regarded as the benchmark modern English rose in American gardens.
name_origin: Named for Olivia Rose Austin, granddaughter of rose breeder David Austin.

description: Olympiad is a bright medium-red hybrid tea rose famous for its non-fading color in summer heat, producing 4 to 5 inch high-centered blooms on long cutting stems. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall with disease-resistant foliage, this 1984 AARS winner was the official rose of the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games and remains a top exhibition and cutting rose.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Olympiad' is a brilliant red hybrid tea rose bred by Canadian-born breeder Sam McGredy IV in New Zealand in 1982, named for the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Games where it was the official rose. It won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1984 and remains a standard for pure, non-fading, sun-resistant crimson in modern rose gardens.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Olympiad' is a vivid medium-red hybrid tea rose bred by Northern Irish-born New Zealand hybridizer Sam McGredy IV, released in 1982 from a cross between 'Red Planet' and 'Pharaoh'. The Los Angeles Olympic Organizing Committee selected the cultivar as the official rose of the 1984 Games, and the entire marathon route was lined with it. 'Olympiad' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1984 and the Portland Gold Medal the same year, earning a reputation as one of the most reliable reds ever bred: the blooms hold their brilliant clear crimson in strong sun without fading or purpling, and the plant resists disease better than most older reds.

Light tea-rose fragrance. Long stems make it a superb cut flower. Still widely grown by American exhibitors for its near-perfect classic form and heat-tolerant color.

description: Rosa 'Oso Easy Double Red' is a compact landscape rose with clusters of fully double red flowers on a rounded, easygoing shrub. It stays about 60-90 cm tall, repeats through the warm season, and was selected for the disease resistance modern home gardeners need more than complicated spray schedules. The flowers have a traditional rose shape at a smaller scale, making the plant useful near paths, patios, low borders, and mass plantings. Full sun and well-drained soil give the best bloom, while simple spring pruning keeps the shrub dense. It brings the look of a classic red rose into the practical world of everyday landscape planting.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Oso Easy Double Red' is a compact landscape shrub rose bred by David Zlesak in the United States and released by Proven Winners in the 2010s. It produces continuous clusters of fully double bright red blooms on an exceptionally disease-resistant plant, part of the Oso Easy series designed specifically for no-spray low-maintenance gardening.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Oso Easy Double Red' is a compact shrub rose bred by American hybridizer David C. Zlesak and released by Proven Winners ColorChoice as part of the Oso Easy series marketed for extremely easy landscape use. Zlesak, based in Minnesota, selected the cultivar specifically for resistance to multiple black spot races, powdery mildew, and extreme winter hardiness, using modern molecular screening combined with traditional multi-year disease-pressure field trials. 'Oso Easy Double Red' produces continuous clusters of fully double bright red blooms from late spring to heavy frost on compact mounded plants 60 to 90 centimeters tall, and the cultivar requires no spraying and no deadheading.

The series competes with Knock Out roses in the no-fuss landscape market, with sibling cultivars in pink, cherry pink, and peach. Bred by Chris Warner in England and introduced by Proven Winners in the 2010s as part of the Oso Easy series.

Combines old-fashioned rose form with cutting-edge disease resistance, a top performer in independent All-America Rose Selections and American Garden Rose Selections trials.
name_origin: Named 'Oso Easy' (Spanish/English pun on 'oh so easy') to highlight its exceptionally low-maintenance habit.

In the modern landscape, this is the rose of the busy life, a red bloom that asks only that someone, occasionally, walk past.

description: Pascali is a classic white hybrid tea rose considered one of the best whites ever bred, producing elegant 4-inch high-centered blooms on tall straight stems. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall with dark green foliage, mildly fragrant, it was voted 'World's Favorite Rose' by the World Federation of Rose Societies in 1991 and remains a top wedding and cutting rose in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Pascali' is a pure white hybrid tea rose bred by Belgian breeder Louis Lens in 1963, a cross between 'Queen Elizabeth' and 'White Butterfly'. It won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1969 and the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 1991, recognized as one of the finest white hybrid teas ever bred.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Pascali' is a pure white hybrid tea rose bred by Belgian hybridizer Louis Lens of Wavre-Notre-Dame, released in 1963 from a cross between the pink 'Queen Elizabeth' and the ivory 'White Butterfly'. Named for the Belgian film Mr. Pascal, the cultivar produces long-stemmed high-centered creamy-white blooms with faint pink flush at the base of petals, making it a premier commercial cut flower for decades. 'Pascali' won the Royal National Rose Society's President's International Trophy in 1967, the All-America Rose Selections award in 1969, the Golden Rose of The Hague in 1973, and induction into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 1991.

Its clean white color, reliable disease resistance, and durable stems keep it in commerce over sixty years later. Bred by Louis Lens in Belgium in 1963 and introduced to America shortly after.

Won the World's Favorite Rose award in 1991 and remains a benchmark for white hybrid tea quality. A top commercial cut flower for American wedding florists due to its pure color and long vase life.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Paul Shirville' is a salmon-pink hybrid tea rose bred by Pat Dickson of Dickson Roses in Northern Ireland and released by Harkness Roses in Hertfordshire, England, in 1983 from a cross involving 'Compassion' and 'Mischief'. The name honored engineer Paul Shirville on his retirement from Harkness's distribution warehouse. The classic high-centered blooms open warm salmon-pink with coppery undertones and a strong, sweet, rich fragrance evoking traditional old-rose and honeyed fruit notes.

'Paul Shirville' won the Edland Fragrance Medal in 1982, the James Mason Gold Medal in 1989 (awarded every five years to a rose that has given great pleasure for at least fifteen years), and remains a popular British garden and cut-flower cultivar. Disease resistance and vigorous upright habit make it an excellent exhibition and landscape rose.

Named for a retired engineer and rose enthusiast, it remains a classic fragrance rose in both English and American gardens.

description: Peace is the most famous hybrid tea rose in history, producing huge 5 to 6 inch high-centered blooms of pale yellow edged with pink on vigorous 4 to 6 foot bushes. Mildly fragrant with glossy dark green foliage, it set the standard for modern hybrid teas and remains a beloved American garden rose generations after its 1945 introduction.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Peace' is a hybrid tea rose bred by Francis Meilland at Cap d'Antibes in 1935. Budwood reached Conard-Pyle in Pennsylvania days before France fell in 1940; the rose was launched in 1945 and renamed 'Peace' on the day Berlin fell, with blooms given to delegates at the UN's founding in San Francisco.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Peace' is a hybrid tea rose bred by French breeder Francis Meilland at Cap d'Antibes in 1935 from a complex cross involving 'George Dickson', 'Souvenir de Claudius Pernet', and other parents. Meilland recognized its quality and sent budwood to colleagues in Italy, Germany, Turkey, and the United States. The American consignment, delivered to Conard-Pyle in Pennsylvania on the last American diplomatic flight out of Lyon in 1940, reached Robert Pyle days before France fell to Germany.

Pyle introduced the rose in 1945 and the All-America Rose Selections renamed it 'Peace' on the day Berlin fell; a bloom was given to each delegate at the founding of the United Nations in San Francisco. Officially introduced in America on April 29, 1945, the day Berlin fell, and named 'Peace' to commemorate the end of the war.

Became the best-selling rose in history and a symbol of post-war hope. The cultivar remains one of the most widely grown roses in history.
name_origin: Named 'Peace' in 1945 to mark the end of World War II; known as 'Madame A. Meilland' in France after the breeder's mother.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Perfume Delight' is a medium pink hybrid tea rose bred by Herb Swim and O. L. Weeks in California in 1973. Named for its intense old-rose fragrance, it won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1974 and remains prized by home gardeners for its sweet damask scent and large perfectly formed high-centred pink blooms on vigorous upright plants.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Perfume Delight' is a medium pink hybrid tea rose bred by American hybridizers Herb Swim and O. L. Weeks, released by Armstrong Roses in 1973 from a complex cross involving 'Peace', 'Happiness', 'Chrysler Imperial', and 'El Capitan'. The large classic high-centered blooms open from pointed buds to velvety warm-pink flowers up to thirteen centimeters across, carried on long straight stems above dark green foliage. As its name suggests, the cultivar's strongest selling point is its fragrance, an intense old-rose damask-and-spice scent that won it the All-America Rose Selections award in 1974.

'Perfume Delight' has proved vigorous and disease-resistant in American gardens and remains a reliable cut flower and exhibition rose fifty years after introduction. Bred by Ollie Weeks in California and introduced by Weeks Roses in 1973, winning AARS in 1974.

Bred specifically to recapture the intense perfume of old-fashioned roses in a modern hybrid tea form, it remains a fragrance-garden favorite in American collections.
name_origin: Named 'Perfume Delight' for its powerful old-rose fragrance that delights the senses.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Pink Knock Out' is a medium-pink shrub rose released in 2004 by William Radler and Conard-Pyle as a colour sport of the revolutionary 'Knock Out'. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Pink Knock Out' is a clear medium-pink shrub rose released in 2004 by William J. Radler and Conard-Pyle as a color sport of the original cherry-red 'Knock Out'. The single to semi-double bright pink blooms show a white eye at the base of the petals and ring of golden stamens, blooming continuously from spring to frost on the same compact, mounded, nearly disease-free plants that made the original so successful. The cultivar extended the Knock Out series into a color already popular in the landscape trade and became one of the best-selling pink roses in North America.

Like its parent, it requires no deadheading, tolerates drought, resists black spot and powdery mildew, and survives into USDA zone 4 without winter protection. Extended the Knock Out color range and brought disease-resistant pink landscape roses to American home gardens.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Pink Promise' is a soft pink hybrid tea rose registered in 2009 by Canadian hybridizer Brad Jalbert of Select Roses, released commercially by Jackson & Perkins. Jackson & Perkins partnered with the National Breast Cancer Foundation and designated a portion of every sale to the charity, intentionally creating a horticultural symbol of breast-cancer awareness at a time when pink-ribbon campaigns were reaching their peak. The classic high-centered blooms open from pointed buds to large wide flowers in shades of light to medium pink, carried on long straight stems above semi-glossy dark green foliage.

A light old-rose fragrance complements the color. 'Pink Promise' is vigorous, moderately disease-resistant, and widely planted in memorial gardens, hospital plantings, and residential gardens.

Introduced in 2009 as a joint effort between Edmunds Roses and the National Breast Cancer Foundation. A portion of every sale supports breast cancer awareness and research, making it one of the most meaningful commemorative roses in America.

A modern classic since its 1976 introduction, it remains one of the most vivid and cheerful floribunda roses in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Playboy' is a vivid multicoloured floribunda rose bred by Scottish hybridizer Alec Cocker of James Cocker & Sons in Aberdeen, released in 1976 from a cross between 'City of Leeds' and ('Chanelle' x 'Piccadilly').
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Playboy' is a vivid multicoloured floribunda rose bred by Scottish hybridizer Alec Cocker of James Cocker & Sons in Aberdeen, released in 1976 from a cross between 'City of Leeds' and ('Chanelle' x 'Piccadilly'). The single to semi-double blooms, just seven to twelve wavy petals around a boss of golden stamens, open with yellow bases that flush into bright scarlet-orange at the tips, giving flowers a glowing flame effect unmatched among floribundas. Large clusters on vigorous upright plants cover the bush through the season.

'Playboy' won the Gold Medal at Portland in 1989 and remains a favorite for bold garden color, landscape beds, and mass plantings; its glossy disease-resistant foliage and free-flowering habit make it reliable even in indifferent care. Light tea fragrance. Famous for its flame-colored yellow-orange-red blend that changes as flowers age.
name_origin: Named 'Playboy' to convey the flashy flame-colored cheerful personality of the flowers.

It is the rose that refuses to apologize for being loud, and gardens are better for it unrepentant brightness.

description: Popcorn is a classic miniature rose bred by Dennison Morey and introduced in 1973, beloved for its clusters of tiny white semi-double blooms with bright yellow stamens that truly resemble popped popcorn kernels. Growing just 12 to 14 inches tall in a neat rounded shape, it blooms continuously from spring through frost with a light honey fragrance. history_text_short: Rosa 'Popcorn' is a tiny white miniature rose bred by American hybridizer Dennison Morey in 1973, a cross of 'Katharina Zeimet' and 'Diamond Jewel'. Clusters of small semi-double white blooms with golden stamens resemble popcorn kernels, giving the rose its name and lasting container popularity.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Popcorn' is a white miniature rose bred by American hybridizer Dennison H. Morey, released in 1973 from a cross between the polyantha 'Katharina Zeimet' and the miniature 'Diamond Jewel'. The cultivar produces enormous clusters of twenty to thirty small semi-double blooms, each just 2.5 centimeters across with a cluster of golden stamens at the centre of pure white ruffled petals; the massed effect on the compact 40-centimeter plant does indeed resemble popcorn kernels scattered across the foliage, hence the name. 'Popcorn' blooms continuously from late spring to heavy frost with a light honey scent, and has proved extremely popular for containers, front-of-border plantings, and miniature rose collections.

A sport called 'Gourmet Popcorn' released in 1986 is larger, more vigorous, and has largely replaced the original in commerce. Its sport 'Gourmet Popcorn' (1986) became even more widely grown, but the original Popcorn remains a cherished mini in American rose collections.
name_origin: Cultivar name evokes the small rounded white blooms with yellow centers resembling freshly popped popcorn kernels.

description: Princess Anne is a David Austin English rose introduced in 2010, producing deep rich-pink rosette blooms with yellow backs on petals that shift to softer pink as they age, carrying a medium tea fragrance. Growing 3 to 4 feet in an unusually tidy compact upright shrub, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall with exceptional disease resistance. A modern Austin rose for small American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Princess Anne' is a deep pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2010 and named with permission of Her Royal Highness The Princess Royal. Rosette-shaped blooms open rich deep pink with yellow petal reverses, fading through rose to lilac-pink as they age. The compact, exceptionally disease-resistant plant blooms continuously on dense upright growth.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Princess Anne' is a deep pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2010 from proprietary parentage, named with the consent of Her Royal Highness Princess Anne, The Princess Royal, who is an active patron of rural and horticultural charities. The medium-sized rosette-shaped fully double blooms, seven to eight centimeters across, open a rich deep pink with yellow petal reverses and fade gradually through rose to lilac-pink as flowers age, so plants display multiple tones simultaneously. Moderate old-rose fragrance with light tea notes.

The cultivar's standout quality is its dense upright bushy growth, exceptional disease resistance, and compact scale (1.1 meters tall), making 'Princess Anne' one of the easiest English Roses to grow well and a reliable choice for mixed borders. Bred by David Austin and introduced in 2010 in honor of HRH Princess Anne, daughter of Queen Elizabeth II and a lifelong supporter of British horticulture.

Its compact habit and disease resistance have made it a top Austin choice for small American cottage gardens.
name_origin: Named for HRH Princess Anne, Princess Royal (b. 1950), daughter of Queen Elizabeth II.

description: Queen Elizabeth is the founding and most famous grandiflora rose, producing 4-inch clear medium-pink high-centered blooms singly or in clusters on tall 5 to 7 foot stems. Mildly fragrant, extremely vigorous, and one of the most award-winning roses in history including the 1955 AARS and World Rose Hall of Fame induction in 1979, it remains a signature American garden rose.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Queen Elizabeth' is a medium-pink grandiflora rose bred by American breeder Dr. Walter Lammerts in 1954, a cross between 'Charlotte Armstrong' and 'Floradora'. Introduced to mark the 1952 coronation of Queen Elizabeth II, its tall stately habit and classic high-centred pink blooms prompted the creation of the entirely new grandiflora class.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Queen Elizabeth' is a tall medium-pink rose bred by American hybridizer Dr. Walter Lammerts at Germain Seed and Plant Company, released in 1954 from a cross between the red 'Charlotte Armstrong' and the pink 'Floradora'. The cultivar was released to commemorate the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom in 1952, with permission of Buckingham Palace. Blooms combined the classic high-centered form of a hybrid tea with the cluster production of a floribunda on an unprecedented two-meter-tall plant; the American Rose Society created an entirely new class, grandiflora, to accommodate it.

'Queen Elizabeth' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1955, the American Rose Society's National Gold Medal Certificate in 1960, and was voted World's Favorite Rose in 1978. It remains one of the most widely grown roses in history.

Walter Lammerts in California and introduced in 1954 to honor Queen Elizabeth II's coronation. Won AARS in 1955 and World Rose Hall of Fame in 1979.

symbolism_story: The Queen Elizabeth Rose can symbolize royal dignity, a stately tribute to Queen Elizabeth II whose tall, well-clothed pink blooms helped define mid-century ideas of garden composure. Another layer is its place as a class founder, for it was the first rose officially designated a grandiflora, between hybrid tea and floribunda. In the historical rose garden, Queen Elizabeth is both monarch and category-maker, a flower whose name and structure together opened a new room in the rose's modern taxonomy.

description: Queen of Sweden is a David Austin English rose introduced in 2004, known for its exquisitely formed upright-facing soft pink blooms of classic old-rose cup form on an unusually upright tidy 4 foot shrub. The flowers open as full half-cups of delicate pink fading to blush, carrying a light myrrh fragrance. Its uncommonly neat upright habit makes it ideal for formal borders and small American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Queen of Sweden' is a soft apricot-blush English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2004, named to celebrate the 350th anniversary of the 1654 treaty between Sweden and England. Upright neat habit with perfectly formed cupped flowers of pale apricot-pink makes it one of the most elegant Austin roses for formal mixed-border plantings.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Queen of Sweden' is a soft apricot-blush English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2004 from proprietary parentage. Austin released the rose to commemorate the 350th anniversary of the 1654 treaty of alliance between Sweden and England signed during the reign of Queen Christina. Unlike the arching or mounded habit of most English Roses, 'Queen of Sweden' is strikingly upright and narrow, suiting formal border use, tight garden designs, and even large containers.

The perfectly cupped rosette-shaped blooms, six to eight centimeters across, open soft warm apricot and fade to clear pale pink with age, carried on the slender upright canes with glossy disease-resistant mid-green foliage. Light old-rose fragrance with myrrh notes.

The plant blooms continuously and shows good disease resistance, and it has become one of the most popular later Austin introductions for its refined habit. Bred by David Austin and introduced in 2004 to commemorate the 350th anniversary of the 1654 treaty between Sweden and Great Britain, honoring Queen Christina of Sweden.
name_origin: Named for Queen Christina of Sweden, to mark 350 years since the 1654 Anglo-Swedish Treaty of Uppsala.

description: Rainbow Knock Out is a unique coral-pink with yellow center version of the original Knock Out, producing clusters of 3-inch single blooms on a compact 3-foot bush. Introduced in 2007, it is the first single-flowered Knock Out and brings pollinator-accessible open blooms with the classic Knock Out disease resistance to American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Rainbow Knock Out' is a bicoloured coral-pink-and-yellow shrub rose released in 2007 by William Radler and Conard-Pyle, the fourth release in the revolutionary Knock Out series. Single blooms have yellow centres flushing outward into coral-pink petal tips, giving a rainbow effect, and the cultivar shares the series' legendary disease resistance.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Rainbow Knock Out' is a bicoloured coral-pink and yellow shrub rose released in 2007 by William J. Radler and Conard-Pyle as the fourth major introduction in the Knock Out series after the original red, Double Knock Out, and Pink Knock Out. The single five-petalled blooms open with clear yellow centres and a tuft of golden stamens, the petal tips suffused with deepening coral-pink so each flower resembles a miniature sunset. The series' trademark qualities are preserved: continuous self-cleaning bloom from spring to heavy frost, minimal black spot or powdery mildew without spraying, cold hardiness to zone 5, and a compact rounded plant suitable for small gardens, mass landscape plantings, or containers.

Like other Knock Outs it requires almost no maintenance beyond an early-spring hard pruning. Bred by William Radler and introduced by Conard-Pyle in 2007 as the first single-flowered rose in the Knock Out series.

Brought open flower form and pollinator support to the iconic landscape rose family.
name_origin: Named 'Rainbow' for the coral-pink petals with yellow eye, creating a two-tone rainbow appearance.

This is the rose for unfussy gardens — easy, sociable, and welcoming to both human visitors and the small creatures that share the border.

Producing small high-centered double blooms in spectacular yellow centers with red petal edges that intensify in sun, the plant grows 12 to 18 inches and blooms continuously from spring through frost. history_text_short: Rosa 'Rainbow's End' is a bicoloured yellow-and-red miniature rose bred by American breeder Harmon Saville in 1984, one of the most celebrated miniature roses ever introduced. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Rainbow's End' is a bicoloured yellow-and-red miniature rose bred by American hybridizer Harmon Saville at Nor'East Miniature Roses in Massachusetts, released in 1984 from a cross between 'Rise 'n' Shine' and 'Watercolor'. The perfect miniature hybrid-tea-shaped blooms, just four centimeters across, open a clear deep yellow and develop intense red flushing at the petal edges proportional to sun exposure, so plants grown in strong sun display a remarkable rainbow effect with buds, half-open blooms, and mature flowers showing every color transition simultaneously. 'Rainbow's End' won the American Rose Society's Award of Excellence in 1986 and became the most celebrated miniature rose of its generation, frequently described as the single most beautiful miniature ever bred.

The compact plant reaches 40 centimeters and blooms continuously; faint scent.

description: Sally Holmes is a world-renowned shrub rose bred by English amateur Robert Holmes in 1976, producing massive trusses of single creamy-white flowers with golden stamens on an arching 6 to 8 foot shrub. Each open bloom resembles an apple blossom, and the plant can carry hundreds of flowers at once from late spring through fall. Exceptionally disease-resistant and beloved in American gardens from coast to coast.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Sally Holmes' is a single-flowered shrub rose bred by English amateur Robert Holmes in 1976 and named for his wife, a cross between 'Ivory Fashion' and 'Ballerina'. Enormous corymbs of up to forty large single creamy-white blooms with pink flushes cover the arching plant continuously, and it was voted into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2012.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Sally Holmes' is a single-flowered shrub rose bred by English amateur hybridizer Robert A. Holmes of Nottinghamshire, released in 1976 from a cross between the floribunda 'Ivory Fashion' and the hybrid musk 'Ballerina'. Holmes named the rose for his wife Sally. The arching shrubby plant produces enormous corymbs of up to forty flowers, each a wide five-petalled single bloom of creamy white faintly flushed pink at the bud stage, centered on a prominent tuft of golden stamens; open trusses resemble small bouquets of single white dogwoods.

'Sally Holmes' won the Royal National Rose Society's Gold Medal, Baden-Baden Gold Medal, Portland Gold Medal, and in 2012 was voted into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame. Light sweet musky fragrance; excellent as a specimen, climber, or mass-planting.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Savoy Hotel' is a light pink hybrid tea rose bred by Pat Dickson of Dickson Roses in Northern Ireland and released in 1987 from a cross between 'Silver Jubilee' and 'Amber Queen', to mark the centenary of the Savoy Hotel in London. The classic high-centered blooms open from elegant pointed buds to wide flowers in shades of light pink with a slightly darker rose-pink petal reverse, held singly on long straight stems above glossy disease-resistant dark green foliage. The plant is tall, upright, and vigorous, repeats almost continuously through the summer, and tolerates British weather unusually well.

Light to moderate sweet fragrance. 'Savoy Hotel' won the 1988 Dublin Gold Medal and remains one of the best-selling pink hybrid teas for UK garden centres and cut-flower growers.

Bred by Harkness Roses and introduced in 1989 to commemorate the centennial of London's luxurious Savoy Hotel. Known for its consistent bloom form and clean foliage, it has become a favorite of American gardeners seeking a reliable soft-pink hybrid tea.

description: Scarlet Meidiland is a low-growing spreading mini landscape rose from Meilland's Meidiland series, introduced in 1987, producing abundant small bright scarlet-red double flowers in clusters on a sprawling 3 foot plant. history_text_short: Rosa 'Scarlet Meidiland' is a bright cherry-scarlet groundcover shrub rose bred by Marie-Louise Meilland at the Meilland nursery near Antibes, France, released in 1987 as part of the pioneering Meidiland landscape series.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Scarlet Meidiland' is a bright cherry-scarlet groundcover shrub rose bred by Marie-Louise Meilland at the Meilland nursery near Antibes, France, released in 1987 as part of the pioneering Meidiland landscape series. The arching wide-spreading plant reaches 1.2 meters tall and 1.8 meters wide, and produces enormous clusters of twenty to forty small semi-double bright scarlet blooms continuously from late spring to heavy frost, creating a dramatic sheet-of-color effect. Along with its Meidiland siblings (white, pink, red), it helped establish the modern easy-care landscape shrub rose category in the 1980s, before the later Knock Out and Drift revolutions.

The cultivar requires no spraying, tolerates heat, drought, and cold into USDA zone 4, and is widely used in municipal median plantings, commercial landscape beds, and slope stabilization. Its small scale and sprawling habit make it a versatile container and edging rose in American gardens.
name_origin: 'Meidiland' is a Meilland trademark for the landscape rose series; 'Scarlet' describes the bright red flower color.

description: Scentimental is a unique striped burgundy-and-cream floribunda rose with strong sweet spicy fragrance, producing 4-inch semi-double blooms with no two alike. Growing 3 to 4 feet tall, this 1997 AARS winner was one of the first modern striped roses widely available and remains an eye-catching novelty floribunda in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Scentimental' is a striped burgundy-and-cream floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in Upland, California, released in 1996 from a cross between 'Playboy' and 'Peppermint Twist'.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Scentimental' is a striped burgundy-and-cream floribunda bred by Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in Upland, California, and released in 1996. Its parentage includes 'Playboy' and 'Peppermint Twist', a pairing that helped revive the old fascination with striped roses.

Every bloom opens with a different swirl of wine-red and creamy white, so the plant never looks exactly the same from one flower to the next. Carruth's aim was not novelty alone: 'Scentimental' also carries a strong old-rose-and-spice fragrance and relatively clean modern foliage.

The cultivar won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1997 and remains popular because it makes pattern part of the story. It brought the romance of historic striped roses, such as 'Rosa Mundi', into a modern repeat-flowering floribunda.
name_origin: Name 'Scentimental' puns on 'sentimental' to highlight its strong fragrance and romantic striped petals.

description: Sexy Rexy is a top-tier light pink floribunda rose producing large sprays of 3-inch fully double rosette blooms on a 3 to 4 foot bush. Mildly fragrant with excellent disease resistance, this 1989 New Zealand-bred rose was inducted into the World Rose Hall of Fame in 2006 and remains a benchmark pink floribunda in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Sexy Rexy' is a medium-pink floribunda bred by New Zealand's Sam McGredy IV in 1984, a cross of 'Seaspray' and 'Dreaming'. Huge sprays of up to thirty flat camellia-like blooms per cluster made it one of the most awarded floribundas, including the World Rose Hall of Fame in 2006.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Sexy Rexy' is a medium pink floribunda rose bred by Sam McGredy IV in New Zealand, released in 1984 from a cross between 'Seaspray' and 'Dreaming'. The name, a tribute to New Zealand breeder Rex Gourlay, caught publishers by surprise but the cultivar's performance silenced any quibbles: huge sprays of twenty to thirty camellia-like blooms per cluster, each flat and many-petalled in clear medium pink, cover the compact plant continuously through the season. 'Sexy Rexy' won the New Zealand Gold Star, Auckland Gold Medal, Portland Gold Medal, Glasgow Gold Medal, and was inducted into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 2006, making it one of the most decorated floribundas in history.

Light spicy fragrance; disease-resistant and cold-hardy. The playful name caused publishing controversy but did not prevent it becoming one of the most widely-grown pink floribundas in American and international gardens.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Sheer Bliss' is a blush pink hybrid tea rose bred by American hybridizer William A. Warriner at Jackson & Perkins in Medford, Oregon, released in 1985 from a cross between 'White Masterpiece' and 'Grand Masterpiece'. The unusually long, spiralled pointed buds open slowly to large high-centered blooms of creamy white with a delicate pink heart, held on long straight stems perfect for exhibition and cut-flower work. A clear spicy fragrance with notes of clove and honey added to the rose's appeal.

'Sheer Bliss' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1987 and became a favorite of wedding and special-event florists through the 1990s for its refined color and classic form. The plant is vigorous and moderately disease-resistant, best in warmer climates.

Bred by William Warriner at Jackson & Perkins and introduced in 1985, winning AARS in 1987. A frequent exhibition winner, it set a new standard for pale-pink hybrid tea form in American rose shows of the late 1980s and remains a wedding-florist favorite.

history_text_long:
Rosa 'Showbiz' is a vivid medium-red floribunda rose bred by Mathias Tantau Jr. at Uetersen, Germany, released in 1981 from proprietary parentage. The compact plant produces huge trusses of up to thirty semi-double medium-red blooms, each about eight centimeters across with a central boss of golden stamens, continuously from late spring to heavy frost. Exceptional glossy disease-resistant dark green foliage, cold hardiness, and the dense carpet-of-color effect made 'Showbiz' an immediate landscape favorite.

It won Gold Medals at Baden-Baden and The Hague and the All-America Rose Selections award in 1985, placing it among the most celebrated red floribundas of the 1980s. Light fragrance; performs well in public plantings, mass beds, and small gardens with minimal care. Bred by Mathias Tantau Jr. in Germany and introduced in 1981, winning AARS in 1985.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Simplicity' is a medium pink floribunda rose bred by William Warriner at Jackson & Perkins in 1978. history_text_long:
Rosa 'Simplicity' is a medium pink floribunda rose bred by American hybridizer William A. Warriner at Jackson & Perkins in Medford, Oregon, released in 1978 from a cross between an unnamed seedling and 'Iceberg'. Jackson & Perkins marketed the cultivar aggressively as the Living Fence rose, encouraging gardeners to plant rows of bare-root bushes as flowering hedges, and the campaign combined with 'Simplicity's' easy-care habit drove it to become one of the best-selling roses in North America through the 1980s and 1990s. The clusters of semi-double clear medium pink blooms appear continuously on upright vigorous plants with good disease resistance.

Light tea fragrance. Later sports including 'Red Simplicity', 'White Simplicity', and 'Yellow Simplicity' extended the series into other colours.

Bred by William Warriner at Jackson & Perkins and introduced in 1978. Marketed as 'the living fence' in the late 1970s, it revolutionized American home landscape design with its hedge-forming habit, disease resistance, and continuous bloom.

history_text_short: Rosa 'Souvenir de la Malmaison' is a blush-pink Bourbon rose bred by French breeder Jean Beluze in 1843, named to honour Empress Josephine's legendary rose garden at Château de Malmaison which had been destroyed by that date. Perfectly quartered pale blush blooms with a rich tea fragrance made it one of the most cherished old roses of the Victorian era.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Souvenir de la Malmaison' is a blush-pink Bourbon rose bred by French hybridizer Jean Beluze, released in 1843 from a cross between the tea rose 'Madame Desprez' and an unnamed tea. The Grand Duke of Russia commissioned the name to honor the memory of Château de Malmaison, Empress Josephine Bonaparte's estate outside Paris where she had assembled the world's most comprehensive rose collection (over 250 cultivars) before her death in 1814; by 1843 the gardens had been largely destroyed. The fully double flat-quartered blooms, twelve centimeters across, open a rich creamy blush pink and pale to near white in sun, carrying a rich tea-and-spice fragrance regarded as among the finest in the old-rose canon.

Repeat bloom throughout the season on a compact bourbon-style shrub; a climbing sport released in 1893 extends its use. Sensitive to rain and mildew but indispensable in heritage rose gardens.

Bred by Jean Beluze in Lyon, France in 1843, the rose was reportedly named when a Grand Duke of Russia acquired it for the Imperial Gardens in St. It became one of the most beloved Bourbon roses in American Victorian gardens.

history_text_short: Rosa 'St. Patrick' is an unusual yellow hybrid tea rose bred by Texan breeder Frank Strickland in 1996 with a distinctive green cast on the outer petals, most pronounced in hot sunny weather. history_text_long:
Rosa 'St. Patrick' is a warm yellow hybrid tea rose bred by amateur Texas hybridizer Frank Strickland, released in 1996 from a cross between 'Brandy' and 'Gold Medal'. The cultivar's distinguishing feature is the faint emerald-green cast on the outer petals of newly opened blooms, most pronounced in hot weather and strong sunlight, giving flowers a uniquely cool quality unusual among yellow roses. Inner petals open clear gold to lemon-yellow, fading slowly to cream.

'St. Patrick' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1996, a rare honor for an amateur breeder's introduction, and became popular across the southern United States for its exceptional heat tolerance and long-lasting cut flowers. Named for the Irish saint and the distinctive green tint of its petals. Light tea fragrance; vigorous upright habit.

description: Sterling Silver is a legendary lavender hybrid tea rose that pioneered silvery-mauve color in modern roses, producing 4-inch blooms with a strong citrusy fragrance. Growing 3 to 4 feet tall on a moderate bush, it established the lavender rose category in 1957 and remains a collector's favorite for its unique coloring and powerful scent.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Sterling Silver' is a lavender hybrid tea rose bred by Gladys Fisher in California in 1957, one of the first commercially successful mauve roses. Though moderately vigorous, its unusual silvery-lilac colour and strong citrus fragrance made it an enduring sentimental favourite, and it appears in the pedigrees of most modern lavender rose cultivars.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Sterling Silver' is a lavender hybrid tea rose bred by American amateur hybridizer Gladys Fisher in California from a seedling of an unnamed mauve rose, released commercially by Hansen Nursery in 1957. It was among the first commercially successful mauve roses and caused an immediate sensation, its silvery-lilac color completely unlike anything previously available. Although the plant itself is moderately vigorous, disease-prone, and demanding in the garden, 'Sterling Silver' has been tremendously influential as a breeding parent and appears in the pedigree of most modern lavender cultivars including 'Blue Moon', 'Angel Face', and 'Paradise'.

The strong lemon-verbena fragrance was equally unusual. Enthusiasts still grow it for sentimental reasons, and specialist nurseries continue to propagate the original clone.

The first commercially successful lavender hybrid tea rose, it established an entirely new color class that paved the way for dozens of later mauve cultivars.
name_origin: Named 'Sterling Silver' for the flower's distinctive shimmering silvery-lavender color.

It is often read as a flower of color breakthrough, a hybrid tea whose meaning is the moment a new shade became possible, opening a quiet door for every dusky rose that followed.

description: Sun Sprinkles is a modern miniature rose bred by Michael Williams and introduced in 1999, winning both the AARS and ARS Award of Excellence. Producing clear bright yellow double blooms with spicy fragrance on a tidy 18 to 24 inch plant, it blooms continuously from spring through frost. One of few miniatures to win AARS recognition, it remains a top yellow mini in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Sun Sprinkles' is a bright yellow miniature rose bred by Keith Zary at Jackson & Perkins in 1999, one of the rare miniature roses to win the All-America Rose Selections award. Deep clear yellow blooms with good fragrance, exceptional disease resistance, and compact vigorous growth made it a landmark in modern miniature rose breeding.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Sun Sprinkles' is a deep yellow miniature rose bred by Dr. Keith W. Zary at Jackson & Perkins, released in 1999 from proprietary parentage. The cultivar is one of the rare miniatures ever to win the All-America Rose Selections award, receiving the honor in 2001 for its combination of high clean color, exceptional disease resistance, vigorous compact growth, and notable fragrance, all qualities often lacking in commercial miniature cultivars. The perfectly formed hybrid-tea-shaped blooms, just four to five centimeters across, open and hold a rich clear deep yellow without fading to cream, carried on a compact bushy 50-centimeter plant with glossy dark green disease-resistant foliage.

A moderate sweet fragrance, unusual in the miniature class, adds to the appeal. Excellent for small gardens, containers, and the front of mixed borders.

Bred by Michael Williams and introduced in 1999, Sun Sprinkles won both the All-America Rose Selections award (rare for a miniature) and the American Rose Society's Award of Excellence. It remains one of the most celebrated yellow mini roses in American gardens.
name_origin: Cultivar name evokes bright yellow blooms sprinkled across the plant like sunshine.

A reminder that a rose need not be tall to be honored.

description: Sunny Knock Out is a bright yellow version of the original Knock Out, producing clusters of 3-inch semi-double lemon-yellow blooms that fade to cream, with a light sweet fragrance. Growing 3 to 5 feet tall on a rounded bush, introduced in 2008, it is the first fragrant Knock Out and the only yellow in the series.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Sunny Knock Out' is a bright yellow shrub rose released in 2008 by William Radler and Conard-Pyle, extending the Knock Out series into true yellow. Single blooms open clear lemon-yellow and fade to near white, have a stronger sweet fragrance than siblings, and retain the series' hallmark disease resistance and continuous bloom.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Sunny Knock Out' is a bright yellow shrub rose released in 2008 by William J. Radler and Conard-Pyle as the fifth major introduction in the Knock Out series. Unlike its siblings, 'Sunny Knock Out' carries a genuine moderate sweet fragrance, making it the most fragrant Knock Out cultivar. Single to semi-double blooms open clear lemon-yellow with a tuft of golden stamens, fading gradually to cream and finally near white over several days, so plants carry flowers in all stages of color simultaneously.

Compact rounded plants preserve the series' extreme disease resistance, cold hardiness to zone 4, and continuous self-cleaning bloom from late spring to heavy frost. Widely adopted in public-space landscaping because yellow roses of comparable toughness were previously unavailable.

Bred by William Radler and introduced by Conard-Pyle in 2008. The first fragrant rose in the Knock Out series and the only yellow, expanding the color palette with a sweet scent that other Knock Outs lack.
name_origin: Named 'Sunny' for the bright lemon-yellow flower color reminiscent of sunshine.

As a fragrant family member — the first scented rose in the line — it adds a soft sweet perfume to the toughness for which the series is known. Its meaning is unfussy gladness: a low-maintenance shrub that smiles and smells like summer.

description: Sunsprite is a classic deep yellow floribunda rose producing clusters of 3-inch fully double blooms with strong sweet fragrance. Growing 2 to 3 feet tall on a compact bush, famously holding its bright non-fading color in hot summer sun, it won the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal and remains the best yellow floribunda in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Sunsprite' (German: 'Friesia') is a bright yellow floribunda rose bred by Reimer Kordes at W. Kordes' Söhne in Sparrieshoop, Germany, released in 1973 from a cross between 'Friedrich Wörlein' and 'Spanish Sun'.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Sunsprite' (German: 'Friesia') is a bright yellow floribunda rose bred by Reimer Kordes at W. Kordes' Söhne in Sparrieshoop, Germany, released in 1973 from a cross between 'Friedrich Wörlein' and 'Spanish Sun'. The clusters of semi-double clear buttercup-yellow blooms, remarkable in a genus where yellow tends to fade quickly, hold their intense color in sun and rain, and the strong sweet licorice-and-honey fragrance perfumes the garden for meters around. 'Sunsprite' won the American Rose Society's James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 1979, the first floribunda ever to do so, and multiple European trial awards.

The compact plant is disease-resistant, cold-hardy, and among the most continuously blooming yellow roses available. Beloved by cottage and landscape gardeners worldwide.
name_origin: Named 'Sunsprite' in America to evoke its bright sunny yellow color; European name is 'Friesia.'

symbolism_list.description: bright yellow cheer

symbolism_story: Sunsprite Rose is joyful friendship in pure deep yellow — a sunny floribunda chosen for cheerful gifts and cottage borders, the rose you plant when you want the bed to feel hopeful. It also carries fragrance as honor: it won the prestigious Gamble Fragrance Medal, a rarity for a yellow rose. It is sunshine bottled into a hardy shrub, given as a small bright friendship across the garden gate.

description: Tea Clipper is a David Austin English rose introduced in 2006, producing large apricot-pink fully-rosette blooms with a rich tea and myrrh fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet in a bushy shrub or trainable as a short climber, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall. The warm apricot tones and strong fragrance make it a favorite Austin rose for American cottage and English-style gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Tea Clipper' is an apricot-yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2006, named for the 19th-century clipper ships that raced China tea to London. Cupped apricot-yellow blooms carry a strong fruity scent with myrrh hints on a tall upright disease-resistant plant.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Tea Clipper' is an apricot-yellow English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2006 from proprietary parentage. Austin named the cultivar for the legendary nineteenth-century clipper ships, the Cutty Sark, Thermopylae, Taeping, and others, that raced the new China tea crop back to London docks for premium prices, and the rose's warm fragrance recalls both rich tea and the fragrant spices those ships carried. The fully double quartered cupped blooms, ten centimeters across, open in warm shades of apricot and soft yellow, with a strong distinctive tea-and-myrrh fragrance and soft citrus notes.

The tall upright plant reaches 1.5 meters and blooms continuously from late spring to hard frost, with good disease resistance and reliable repeat. A late-mid Austin introduction that suits mixed borders and back-of-border placement where height is welcome.

Bred by David Austin and introduced in 2006, Tea Clipper honors the fast sailing ships that carried tea from China to England in the 19th century. Its warm apricot tones and tea fragrance perfectly evoke its namesake, and it has become a beloved Austin rose in American cottage gardens.
name_origin: Named for 19th-century tea clipper sailing ships that raced tea from China to England, referencing the rose's tea fragrance.

description: The Generous Gardener is a David Austin English rose introduced in 2002, a vigorous repeat-blooming climber producing soft pale-pink cupped blooms with a delicious Old Rose, musk, and myrrh fragrance. Growing 10 to 15 feet as a climber or 5 feet as a shrub, it blooms heavily from late spring through fall with good disease resistance. A top English climbing rose for American pergolas and trellises.
history_text_short: Rosa 'The Generous Gardener' is a soft blush-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin in 2002, trained by many gardeners as a climber to four metres. The perfectly formed cupped pale pink blooms show a creamy heart and reveal golden stamens as they open, with a delicious myrrh-and-musk fragrance praised as among the finest Austin has produced.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'The Generous Gardener' is a soft blush-pink English shrub rose bred by David Austin at Albrighton, England, released in 2002 from proprietary parentage to celebrate the National Gardens Scheme, the British charity that opens private gardens to the public to raise funds for nursing charities. The beautifully formed fully double cupped blooms, ten centimeters across, open a soft blush pink that pales to creamy white as flowers age, revealing a central boss of golden stamens, and carry a complex fragrance praised as among Austin's finest, combining old-rose, musk, and myrrh notes. Though classed as a shrub in the UK, the cultivar typically reaches two to four meters in warmer climates and is most often grown as a climber, covering pillars, walls, and small pergolas with graceful abundance of bloom continuously from late spring to hard frost.

It has become one of the most beloved Austin climbing roses in American gardens.
name_origin: Cultivar name honors the generous private gardeners who open their gardens through the UK National Gardens Scheme for charity.

Its triple fragrance — Old Rose, musk, and myrrh — drapes the air with an unusually layered perfume. In its name and scent both, generosity becomes something one can actually plant.

description: Tiffany is a beloved pink-and-yellow blend hybrid tea rose producing 5-inch pink blooms with a golden-yellow base and strong sweet fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall on a vigorous bush, this 1955 AARS winner and James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal recipient remains one of the most cherished blended hybrid teas in American gardens.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Tiffany' is a two-toned pink and yellow hybrid tea rose bred by American breeder Robert Lindquist in 1954, a cross between 'Charlotte Armstrong' and 'Girona'. Released by Conard-Pyle, it won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1955 and the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 1962 for its strong fruity scent.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Tiffany' is a bicoloured pink-and-yellow hybrid tea rose bred by American hybridizer Robert V. Lindquist at Howard Rose Company, released by Conard-Pyle in 1954 from a cross between 'Charlotte Armstrong' and 'Girona'. The classic high-centered blooms open bright pink with yellow bases that spread outward as flowers age, held on long straight stems above glossy dark green foliage. 'Tiffany' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1955 and the American Rose Society's James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 1962 for its strong sweet fruity fragrance.

The cultivar was a leading commercial cut-flower rose of the late 1950s and 1960s and remains a sentimental favorite in American gardens, often appearing in rose society heritage collections for its classic form and unforgettable scent. Lindquist in California and introduced by Jackson & Perkins in 1954, winning AARS in 1955 and the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 1962.

Named for the famous New York jeweler Tiffany & Co., a name synonymous with American elegance.
name_origin: Named in 1954 for Tiffany & Co., the iconic New York luxury jeweler.

symbolism_story: The Tiffany Rose can symbolize cherished love, named for the famous New York jeweller and clothed in a glamorous pink-and-yellow blend befitting a window display. One layer is luxury, the unapologetic borrowing of a brand that means, for many, the highest tier of romance. Its second is cherished fragrance, for it is a Gamble Fragrance Medal winner, recognised by rose societies for one of the most refined scents in the modern hybrid tea catalogue.

description: Tournament of Roses is a warm coral-pink grandiflora rose producing 4-inch high-centered blooms in small clusters on 4 to 5 foot stems. Lightly fragrant with excellent disease resistance, this 1989 AARS winner was named for the centennial of Pasadena's famous Rose Parade and remains a beloved American commemorative grandiflora.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Tournament of Roses' is a coral-pink grandiflora rose bred by William Warriner at Jackson & Perkins in 1988, named for the Pasadena, California New Year's parade. Classic high-centred warm pink blooms borne in small clusters on upright plants won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1989, the centennial year of the Tournament of Roses Parade.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Tournament of Roses' is a warm coral-pink grandiflora rose bred by American hybridizer William A. Warriner at Jackson & Perkins, released in 1988. Jackson & Perkins partnered with the Pasadena Tournament of Roses Association to release the cultivar in time for the hundredth running of the Tournament of Roses Parade on New Year's Day 1989. The classic high-centered blooms in shades of coral pink with lighter pink reverse open on long straight stems, borne singly or in small clusters of two or three, in the intermediate habit between hybrid tea and floribunda that defines a grandiflora.

'Tournament of Roses' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 1989. Light fragrance; disease-resistant, vigorous, and reliable in home gardens. Long-lasting cut flower.

Bred by William Warriner at Jackson & Perkins and introduced in 1988, winning AARS in 1989. Named to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the Pasadena Tournament of Roses Parade. A classic American commemorative rose for West Coast gardens.
name_origin: Named for the 100th anniversary (1989) of the Pasadena Tournament of Roses Parade in California.

description: Tropicana is a revolutionary fluorescent orange hybrid tea rose that introduced true orange color to modern roses, producing 5-inch high-centered blooms with a sweet fruity fragrance. Growing 4 to 5 feet tall with glossy dark foliage, this 1963 AARS winner glows intensely in the garden and remains among the most famous orange roses ever bred.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Tropicana' is a vivid orange-red hybrid tea rose bred by German breeder Mathias Tantau Jr. in 1960, the first modern rose to display true fluorescent coral-orange colour. Released in Europe as 'Super Star' and in North America as 'Tropicana', it won the AARS award in 1963 and revolutionized breeding goals for vibrant colour.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Tropicana' is a vibrant coral-orange hybrid tea rose bred by German hybridizer Mathias Tantau Jr. at Uetersen, released in Europe in 1960 under the name 'Super Star'. Its fluorescent pinkish-coral color, unlike anything previously seen in roses, created an international sensation: the cultivar won the Royal National Rose Society's President's International Trophy in 1960, the All-America Rose Selections award in 1963 (sold in North America as 'Tropicana'), and was inducted into the World Federation of Rose Societies Hall of Fame in 1988. The high-centered blooms open on long stems making it a premier cut flower, and a strong fruity fragrance earned it the Fragrance Award in 1964.

'Tropicana' reshaped breeding priorities, driving a generation of rose hybridizers to chase ever more vivid color. in Germany in 1960 as 'Super Star,' introduced to the US as 'Tropicana' by Jackson & Perkins in 1962, winning AARS in 1963.
name_origin: Named 'Tropicana' in America to evoke tropical vibrancy; original German name was 'Super Star' for the flower's glowing color.

Coral-orange blooms offer warm spicy fragrance for cutting and display
Neon coral-orange blooms bring midcentury drama to sunny rose beds

symbolism_list.description: glowing vibrant orange
first true orange hybrid tea

symbolism_story: Tropicana makes visible enthusiasm, its glowing fluorescent orange blooms a true mid-century breakthrough in rose breeding. As the first genuinely orange hybrid tea, it electrified gardens that had previously known only red, pink, yellow, and white. This is the rose of bold new color, a flower whose introduction in 1960 felt like an exclamation point in the staid rose catalog — and which still reads, decades later, as pure botanical excitement.

description: Veterans Honor is a deep dark-red hybrid tea rose producing huge 5 to 6 inch long-stemmed high-centered blooms with a light raspberry fragrance. Growing 5 to 6 feet tall with upright vigor and deep green foliage, it is one of the most popular commemorative roses in America, with proceeds benefiting the Fisher House Foundation supporting military families.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Veterans Honor' is a deep dark red hybrid tea rose bred by Keith Zary at Jackson & Perkins in 1999. Selected by American military veterans' groups as the official rose of veterans' tribute gardens, it produces long-stemmed velvety crimson blooms with excellent vase life and a light raspberry fragrance, and a portion of sales supports veterans' charities.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Veterans Honor' is a dark red hybrid tea rose bred by Dr. Keith W. Zary at Jackson & Perkins, released in 1999 from proprietary parentage. Jackson & Perkins partnered with the Walter Reed Army Medical Center and the Veterans of Foreign Wars to select the cultivar as the official commemorative rose for American military veterans, and a portion of every sale supports veteran-care charities. The velvety dark crimson blooms reach thirteen centimeters across on exceptionally long straight stems, making 'Veterans Honor' a premium florist's rose in addition to a garden variety.

A light raspberry fragrance complements the color. A portion of proceeds benefits the Fisher House Foundation, which provides housing for military families during hospital treatment.

Has become an iconic American commemorative rose. The plant is vigorous, upright, and moderately disease-resistant, and the cultivar is widely planted in memorial gardens at veterans' hospitals, cemeteries, and military bases across the United States.
name_origin: Named 'Veterans Honor' in 2000 as a tribute to American military veterans and their sacrifices.

symbolism_story: The Veterans Honor Rose carries honor and sacrifice in its very name, a tribute to military veterans paired with a charitable mission supporting those who served. Its deep red blooms read as both reverence and remembrance. To grow it is to keep a living memorial in the garden — a flower whose meaning is tied not just to beauty but to the people for whom it stands.

description: Wild Blue Yonder is a unique mauve-lavender grandiflora rose with wine-red edges, producing 4-inch ruffled blooms with strong citrusy-sweet fragrance on 4 to 5 foot stems. A 2006 AARS winner bred by Tom Carruth, it is one of the most popular modern lavender roses in American gardens, beloved for its distinctive coloring and powerful scent.
history_text_short: Rosa 'Wild Blue Yonder' is a lavender-purple grandiflora rose bred by Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses in 2004, one of the most deeply purple modern roses. Ruffled mauve-purple blooms with a strong fruity citrus fragrance won the All-America Rose Selections award in 2006 and the James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 2013.
history_text_long:
Rosa 'Wild Blue Yonder' is a deeply pigmented lavender-purple grandiflora rose bred by American hybridizer Tom Carruth at Weeks Roses, released in 2004 from a cross involving 'International Herald Tribune' and 'Stephens' Big Purple'. The ruffled semi-double blooms open in rich shades of violet, magenta, and true purple that intensify in cooler weather, approaching the elusive blue rose many hybridizers have pursued. A strong citrus and fruit fragrance adds to the appeal.

'Wild Blue Yonder' won the All-America Rose Selections award in 2006 (the last AARS class ever chosen before the programme ended) and the American Rose Society's James Alexander Gamble Fragrance Medal in 2013. Tall upright disease-resistant plants produce continuous bloom, and the cultivar has parented subsequent deep-purple introductions. Named after the US Air Force song, evoking the mauve-blue tones of its petals reminiscent of sky and horizon.
name_origin: Named 'Wild Blue Yonder' after the lyrics of the US Air Force song, referencing sky-blue tones in the lavender petals.

uses_list.text: Strong citrusy-sweet fragrance from mauve grandiflora blooms
Wine-edged ruffled flowers on long stems for bouquets
Unusual lavender color anchors mixed borders

symbolism_list.description: Air Force song reference
rare blue-lavender rose color

symbolism_story: Rosa Wild Blue Yonder expresses adventurous spirit, its name lifted directly from the Air Force song and its color reaching for the sky tones that roses traditionally cannot quite manage. Its rare blue-lavender hue carries those sky tones into the garden with hints of magenta and silver. It is often read as a flower of attempted altitude, a grandiflora whose meaning is the cheerful optimism of trying for a color that perhaps does not yet fully exist, and getting close enough to sing about it.

fragrance.notes: The flowers have a powerful damask-raspberry fragrance.
